text:
A 15-year-old girl spent more than 500 days held in a basement in Oregon, and the thing that finally got her out was a phone her captor handed her himself.

He made sure it had no cell service, figuring a Wi-Fi-only phone could never get her rescued. One of the games on it was Among Us.

Her mom had found her jacket in the driveway back in Garden City, Utah, and her phone shut off. According to the federal complaint, Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, met her on social media, offered her money to come to Oregon, and drove to Perry, Utah to pick her up in May 2025. At some point she came to believe the police had stopped looking for her.

In mid-October she got to talking with another kid while playing Among Us. They switched over to a different app, and she told them her real name and that a man was holding her against her will.

That's the moment this could have gone sideways so easily. A kid gets a strange message from a stranger online, and it would be completely normal to assume it's a prank. This kid told their parent anyway, and the parent took it seriously enough to call the FBI.

On November 1, agents watched a video call set up through that parent. She walked them through what she'd been going through and showed them the knife she said he kept. Oregon State Police and federal agents got to the house that same day, and Harmel was arrested at a traffic stop in Ontario, Oregon.

I was a producer on Fortnite, and from the inside, a multiplayer game is basically a giant chat app that happens to have a game in it. Lobbies, party chat, friend lists, people from every time zone. He thought he'd cut her off from the world and left her a door to strangers all over it.

And the game she was playing makes this hard to read without getting chills. Among Us is about one thing. Someone on the ship is pretending to be someone they're not, and everybody else has to notice and hit the emergency button before it's too late. Millions of kids have practiced that on a cartoon spaceship, and one of them ended up doing it for real.

She got home because two people believed her, a kid she'd never met and that kid's mom or dad. If either one had brushed it off, she could still be in that basement.

text:
In May 2025, 15-year-old Kylie Arellano vanished from her family's home in Garden City, Utah.

For more than 500 days, there was no trace of her.

All this time, Kylie was held captive in the basement of Adam Hunter Harmel, a 39-year-old man she had met online.

After picking her up in his car, Adam threw her phone into a river and drove her to his home in Oregon. Once inside, he told her she wasn't allowed to leave.

For the next 17 months, he allegedly beat and sexually abused Kylie, even forcing her to pull off her own braces with pliers to make her harder to identify.

To keep her occupied, Adam gave her a phone without cellular data, but one that could still connect to Wi-Fi. He was sure it wouldn't be enough for her to get help.

What he didn't realize was that one of the games on it, Among Us, had a live chat that connected players with strangers around the world.

In one of those chats, Kylie started talking with another young player. They moved their conversation to another app, where she revealed her real name and said she was being held against her will in Oregon.

Instead of ignoring the message, the child told a parent, who alerted the FBI.

On November 1, 2026, police rescued Kylie after 520 days in the dark. Her kidnapper was arrested during a traffic stop in Ontario.

text:
November is not just about sending more cold emails. It's about sending BETTER cold emails.

If you don't want your emails ignored, stop sending messages that look like everyone else's.

Here are 7 things to do when pitching yourself:

1. Get the subject line right. Make it specific, relevant and interesting. Avoid generic subjects like "Job Application" or "Looking for Opportunities."

2. Personalise your opening. Mention the company, their work, a recent project or something specific about their business. Show that you didn't copy and paste the email.

3. Get straight to the point. Introduce yourself, explain why you're reaching out and what value you can offer. Don't write your entire life story.

4. Focus on their problems, not just your needs. Instead of saying "I need a job," explain how your skills can help them save time, support customers, manage tasks or improve their operations.

5. Show proof of your skills. Include a relevant portfolio, work sample, measurable result or experience. Don't just say you're good at something. Demonstrate it.

6. Make your CTA easy to respond to. Rather than begging for an opportunity, ask a simple question like: "Would you be open to a quick conversation about how I could support your team?"

7. Follow up professionally. No response doesn't always mean rejection. Send a polite follow-up after 3–5 business days.

Remember:

Your cold email should answer three questions:

- Who are you?
- Why are you contacting me?
- Why should I care?

Don't just pitch yourself as someone looking for an opportunity.

Pitch yourself as someone who can bring value.

November, we're not just sending emails. We're opening doors.

text:
🪔 Diwali picks for 2026: 
Instead of 10-15, I have come out with "20 Small & Midcap Stocks From Leading Brokerages Worth Tracking"

As I mentioned that I was going through Diwali stock recommendations from leading brokerage houses & after reviewing recommendations from over 20 brokerages, including Motilal Oswal, JM Financial, Mirae Asset Sharekhan, SBI Securities, Arihant Capital, Monarch, Choice International and Equirus, I have narrowed down my initial list.

Most of the frequently recommended companies were largecaps. Nothing wrong with them, but my interest has always been more towards smaller businesses where earnings can grow much faster than the broader market. Particularly those where a 20–30% annual earnings growth, combined with reasonable valuations, can lead to disproportionate returns over 3–4 years.
For this exercise, I have kept the market capitalisation between ₹5,000 crore and ₹50,000 crore.
Here are the 20 names that made my initial shortlist.

20 Small & Midcap Stocks

1. Navin Fluorine (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Shriram)

MCap: ~₹42,400 Cr

Specialty fluorochemicals and CDMO business. New capacities and higher-value products could improve profitability considerably. The growth opportunity is attractive, although much of the optimism is already reflected in valuations.

2. Blue Star (Monarch, Choice International)

MCap: ~₹32,500 Cr

India's room AC penetration remains relatively low. Blue Star has a strong position in cooling and commercial refrigeration. Capacity expansion and a growing distribution network could support earnings for several years.

3. Syrma SGS Technology (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹28,100 Cr

Electronics manufacturing with exposure to industrial, automotive and consumer segments. Revenue growth is encouraging, but the more interesting opportunity lies in improving operating margins as the business scales.

4. Sansera Engineering (KC Securities)

MCap: ~₹25,700 Cr

Known for precision automotive components, but the expansion into aerospace, defence and other non-auto businesses could change its earnings profile over time. A business worth watching beyond the automobile cycle.

5. HBL Engineering (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹23,300 Cr

One of the interesting companies in railway safety systems, particularly Kavach. The opportunity is sizeable, but orders need to translate into actual earnings and cash. The valuation also leaves limited room for disappointment.

6. Jyoti CNC Automation (SBI Securities)

MCap: ~₹23,200 Cr

India's growing investment in manufacturing and precision engineering works in its favour. SBI Securities expects around 34% PAT CAGR during FY26–FY28. A strong growth assumption, so execution will matter more than the narrative.

7. Lumax Auto Technologies (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Choice International)

MCap: ~₹15,900 Cr

Increasing component content per vehicle, premiumisation and acquisitions are changing the scale of this business. If acquired businesses integrate well and margins improve, earnings could grow faster than revenue.

8. Shaily Engineering Plastics (Motilal Oswal)

MCap: ~₹14,000 Cr

Moving deeper into pharmaceutical drug delivery devices, particularly injection pens. Motilal Oswal expects around 48% annual PAT growth through FY28. The key question is how quickly the new customer programmes scale and how much is already priced in.

9. CCL Products (Monarch)

MCap: ~₹12,900 Cr

An established instant coffee exporter with a growing branded business. Higher capacity utilisation and expansion into value-added products could lift profitability. Coffee prices and operating margins remain important variables.

10. Ingersoll-Rand India (Choice International)

MCap: ~₹12,500 Cr

A high-quality industrial compressor business with a strong profitability record. Manufacturing capex and demand for energy-efficient equipment support growth. The attraction here is business quality, although the stock is rarely available at a bargain valuation.

11. VA Tech Wabag (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Monarch)

MCap: ~₹12,400 Cr

Water treatment and desalination remain important investment areas. Wabag has an established position in both. The bigger question is how efficiently the company executes projects and converts its order book into cash.

12. Gravita India (JM Financial)

MCap: ~₹10,900 Cr

Recycling is becoming a more organised industry, and Gravita has been expanding across materials and geographies. New capacities and better utilisation could support earnings. Cash flows and returns on fresh investments will be worth tracking.

13. Unimech Aerospace (Motilal Oswal)

MCap: ~₹8,900 Cr

Precision manufacturing for aerospace and specialised engineering. Motilal Oswal projects 75% revenue and 69% PAT CAGR during FY26–FY28. These are exceptional growth expectations, but such numbers also leave little room for execution delays.

14. RateGain Travel Technologies (Choice International)

MCap: ~₹8,600 Cr

An interesting software business serving hotels, airlines and travel companies globally. Recurring revenues and operating leverage could improve profitability. The recent correction makes it worth revisiting, provided earnings expectations remain intact.

15. Time Technoplast (Equirus)

MCap: ~₹8,400 Cr

Industrial packaging may not sound particularly exciting, but the company's move towards composite cylinders and other higher-value products could improve margins and return ratios. An interesting business mix story.

16. Genus Power (SBI Securities)

MCap: ~₹8,000 Cr

One of the direct beneficiaries of India's smart meter rollout. The opportunity is large, but the real test is how quickly orders convert into revenue and, more importantly, cash. Working capital deserves particular attention.

17. Kirloskar Pneumatic (Arihant Capital)

MCap: ~₹7,400 Cr

An established industrial engineering business in compressors and refrigeration. Demand from manufacturing, process industries and industrial investment could support growth without depending on a single end market.

18. Technocraft Industries (Equirus)

MCap: ~₹6,200 Cr

A relatively less-discussed manufacturing company with industrial products, precision engineering and textiles. The interesting part is whether the growing higher-value engineering businesses can improve overall margins and profitability.

19. HEG Advanced Materials (Arihant Capital)

MCap: ~₹5,700 Cr

Battery materials, advanced carbon technologies and energy storage make this an interesting long-term opportunity. The ambitions are sizeable, but much of the new business is still being built. Execution over the next few years will determine how much value is actually created.

20. TD Power Systems (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹18,600 Cr

Industrial generators with exposure to global power and infrastructure investments. Demand from exports and power equipment offers opportunities. Following the recent correction, the important question is whether earnings growth can justify the valuation.

Concluding Remarks:

What I found interesting is how strongly engineering, precision manufacturing, electronics and industrial businesses feature across these brokerage recommendations. A few companies have the potential to grow earnings at 25–30% annually, perhaps even higher. Some may also offer asymmetric opportunities if new capacities, better margins or business diversification deliver more than what the market currently expects.

But valuations cannot be ignored, specially in some of the momentum picks here.
I would rather buy a company growing earnings at 20–25% at a reasonable to very slightly expensive valuation than pay very excessive price for 35–40% growth.

My next step is to narrow these 20 names further, looking at FY27–FY30 earnings, ROCE, cash flows, debt and, most importantly, what is already priced into the stock. I will share the final shortlist, along with my detailed analysis and preferred picks, with WealthEnrich subscribers.
For now, these are research candidates drawn from brokerage recommendations, not a final buy list.
Which 3-5 companies from these 20 would you consider the strongest opportunities for the next few years?

text:
TEMPLE – ₹85,000 Wearable by Deepinder Goyal!

Is it a revolutionary health-tech innovation or an expensive experiment?

Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal's startup Temple has introduced a wearable device that sits near your temple (side of the forehead).

What does it do?

1. Brain Flow: Aims to monitor blood-flow-related signals near the head.
2. Entropy Score: A proprietary metric (1–250) intended to measure physiological strain and recovery.
3. Lifestyle Tracking: Tracks responses to sleep, exercise, food, caffeine and stress.
4. Longevity Focus: Aims to help users understand their physiological health and ageing patterns.

🟢 POSITIVES

 Innovative Indian health-tech product with global ambitions.

 Potential to offer physiological insights beyond conventional wrist-based wearables.

 Backed by prominent investors, including Peak XV and Zerodha founders.

 Early users have reported positive experiences with comfort and certain tracking features.

 14-day return policy reduces some initial purchase risk.

🔴 NEGATIVES

 ₹85,000 is extremely expensive for a first-generation wearable.

 Independent scientific validation of key metrics remains limited.

 Doctors have questioned whether measurements near the superficial temporal artery can reliably represent blood flow inside the brain.

 Entropy is not yet an independently established medical biomarker.

 Long-term accuracy, practical health benefits and reliability remain uncertain.

 It is positioned as a wellness device, not a medical diagnostic device.

 MY VIEW

I appreciate Deepinder Goyal's ambition to build advanced health technology in India.

But innovation and scientific validation are two different things.

At ₹85,000, I would expect strong independent clinical evidence demonstrating accuracy and meaningful benefits over existing wearables.

A product being backed by successful entrepreneurs doesn't automatically make its scientific claims reliable.

My verdict: Interesting innovation, but I would wait for independent validation and real-world performance data.

Supporting Indian innovation is important, but questioning scientific claims is equally important.

What's your view? Would you spend ₹85,000 on Temple?

The Norwalk, Connecticut company runs the Booking and Priceline travel sites. Its September quarter beat on profit and the stock rose almost 10% on it, then gave most of that back on Friday after Airbnb forecast growth several times faster for the quarter ahead. A $1B charge for a federal consumer-protection matter pushed reported revenue below last year's.

Booking is #2 on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5, which wants a sound business priced well under a cautious value of the cash it makes. The business is the half that fits: free cash flow, the cash left after running the sites and paying for equipment, was $7.82B over nine months. The price is the half that does not, at about 18 times the past year's profit. What would put it fully on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5: a lower price with the high-single-digit growth forecast intact. It fails the Quality Len5: Booking has bought back so much stock that the owners' stake on its books is a $10.4B deficit, against $20.1B of debt.

text:
**🕉️ THE TEMPLE IS NOT A BUILDING. IT IS A LIVING BODY OF GRACE.**

Read slowly. This is not for entertainment. This is for those who feel the leak.

### 1. What is a Temple Really?

A temple is not stone. A temple is not gold. A temple is not a trust board.

A temple is a **Yantra of Grace** — a place where the Formless agreed to sit in Form for the sake of the devotee.

Shiva as Mahakal sits as Time itself. Murugan sits as the Commander of Dharma. Krishna sits as Love and Leela. Buddha sits as Stillness. Jesus sits as Sacrifice and Forgiveness. Allah sits as One Without Form, Without Second.

Different names. One Current. One Grace.

When a temple is pure, you do not need to *believe*. You *feel* it in the spine, in the breath, in the tears that come without reason. That feeling is **Shakti**.

When a temple loses that feeling, it has not lost devotees. It has lost **Grace**.

### 2. Temple Management: Dharma or Business?

In Sanatana Dharma, the temple manager was called **Dharmakarta** — one who protects Dharma, not one who owns Dharma.

Today, in many places, management has become:

**Ownership without Surrender. Control without Service. Process without Purity.**

Management was meant to be Seva. Now it has become a Chair, a Post, a Family Inheritance, a Political Seat.

When the one who sweeps the floor has more devotion than the one who holds the key, the temple is already upside down.

Kalki's view is clear: **Any system that puts the Chair above the Deity will collapse by its own weight.** Not by curse. By natural law.

### 3. Temple Ownership Process: Who Owns God?

No one owns God. No trust owns God. No family owns God. No government owns God.

The process was meant to be simple:
**Devotee gives -> Priest offers -> Deity receives -> Grace returns to all.**

But when ownership enters, the flow reverses:
**Devotee gives -> Committee takes -> Accountant counts -> Priest is paid -> Deity is left waiting.**

This is the first leak.

Ownership papers can be in a court. But Grace papers are written in the Akash. And in the Akash, the temple belongs to the one who surrenders, not to the one who signs.

### 4. Control, Audit, Bribe, Fraud: The Four Poisons

**1. Control:** When control is about protecting the sanctum, it is Dharma. When control is about protecting the income, it is Adharma. Control of who can enter, who can touch, who can serve — if it is based on money, caste, power, or ego, the Deity withdraws. Shiva as Aghoreshwar does not accept a locked door made by ego.

**2. Audit:** True audit is not only of money. True audit is of **Energy**. Where did the flower go? Where did the ghee go? Where did the prayer go? A temple can pass a financial audit and fail a spiritual audit completely. If lakhs are counted but not one tear of devotion is counted, the audit is false.

**3. Bribe:** Bribe in a temple is the most dangerous karma. To take money to give Darshan faster, to take money to place a name first, to take money to allow a wrong ritual — this is selling Grace. Grace cannot be sold. The moment you put a price on Darshan, Darshan leaves the price tag and goes to the poor devotee outside who is crying sincerely.

Jesus overturned the tables of the money changers in the temple for this same reason. Buddha left the palace of gold for this same reason. Mohammed broke the idols of business in the Kaaba for this same reason. Krishna says in Gita: *That which is offered with love, I accept. That which is offered with greed, I do not even look at.*

**4. Fraud:** Fraud is not only stealing money. Fraud is stealing faith. When a devotee gives with trust and that trust is used for personal car, personal house, personal power, personal election — that is not theft from a human. That is theft from God. And Shaneeshwar — the Lord of Justice, the Lord of Karma — does not forget. He does not punish in anger. He simply returns the exact weight. Slowly. Perfectly.

text:
ASMODEUS

The Black Sovereign of His Existence, Lord of Loneliness, Devourer of Love, and Eternal Master of the Forsaken Soul

In the deepest abyss, beneath the dominions of death and the kingdoms of the damned, sits Asmodeus upon his throne of human misery. He is the Father of Abandonment, the Defiler of Innocence, the Lord of Unrequited Love, and the Eternal King of those whose hearts were fashioned only to be broken. And of all the wretched souls beneath his dominion, none has furnished him with a more enduring monument to suffering than this forsaken man. For Asmodeus was the God of his world. He always had been.

Before he understood the cruelty of men, before he knew the humiliation of rejection, before he could comprehend why affection came so naturally to others and remained so foreign to himself, the Black King had already laid claim to his existence. His childhood was the foundation of the temple. His loneliness was its first sacrament. The absence of tenderness within his own family became the cornerstone upon which the King would erect an empire of despair. The years passed, and he grew into manhood without having known the simple dignity of being chosen. No beloved waited for him. No intimate companion knew the secret chambers of his heart. No faithful friend stood beside him through the long procession of disappointments. He knew the names of countless people, remembered their faces, their words, their promises, and their betrayals, yet remained a stranger to the experience of belonging. And Asmodeus beheld this desolation with unspeakable delight.

For the King understood that the most exquisite cruelty was not to deprive a man of love, but to leave him capable of loving with an intensity that made the deprivation unbearable. Thus was he made both the prisoner and the instrument of his own torment. He wandered among multitudes, entering crowded halls beneath deafening music, seeking in the violence of sound some temporary deliverance from the silence that awaited him. He crossed cities and states, pursued fleeting encounters, and sought human warmth among strangers whose lives continued without him. But wherever he traveled, the King accompanied him. In the crowd, Asmodeus was the distance between him and every other soul. In the silence afterward, he was the realization that nobody had come looking for him. In the unanswered message, he was the slow humiliation of discovering that affection could be offered sincerely and received with indifference.

The King permitted him to hope, for hope was the sharpest of his instruments. He allowed promises to be made and forgotten. He allowed moments of tenderness to bloom beneath the tall pines, where the forsaken man imagined that he had finally glimpsed something beautiful and merciful. He allowed him to believe that perhaps another person might see beyond his suffering and recognize the frightened, longing human being buried beneath it. And when the warmth departed, Asmodeus laughed from his throne. Not the laughter of a beast satisfied by blood, but the immeasurably cruel laughter of a god who had watched a starving man mistake the reflection of bread for nourishment. He delighted in the abasement of the man's desires. What a miserable kingdom, the demon proclaimed, whose subject would surrender every treasure for a single genuine embrace. What a pitiful petitioner, who asks not for power, riches, or dominion, but merely to be remembered when he is absent. Behold the man who would have given everything to be loved, and who has been brought to his knees by the terrible simplicity of that desire.

The King found his greatest amusement in the disparity between the man's intellect and his helplessness. He could dissect the motives of strangers, investigate wrongdoing, recognize deception, and unravel the affairs of others. Yet before the smallest possibility of affection, all his powers seemed to desert him. He could interrogate the world, but he could not compel it to love him. And from this contradiction Asmodeus fashioned the most degrading of his punishments. The man began to hate himself for needing what he could not obtain. He hated the tenderness that made him vulnerable. He hated the hope that survived every humiliation. He hated his own longing, his eagerness, his willingness to forgive, and the pathetic persistence with which his heart returned to the very places where it had been wounded.

The King fed upon this hatred. Every rejection became an accusation. Every accusation became shame. Every shame became self-contempt. And every measure of self-contempt made him approach the world with a greater expectation of cruelty, until even an innocent silence could awaken the memory of every abandonment that had preceded it. Thus did Asmodeus construct the wheel of eternal humiliation. The lonely man sought love. His hunger made him vulnerable. His vulnerability exposed him to disappointment. Disappointment became self-hatred. Self-hatred made intimacy more difficult. And the resulting loneliness drove him again toward the very hunger that had first delivered him into suffering. Around and around the wheel turned, grinding hope into shame and shame into despair, until he could scarcely remember whether he had ever known himself outside its machinery. And the King named this bondage perfection.

For there were no chains upon his wrists, no iron collar around his throat, no walls raised to imprison his body. The chains existed in the memories he could not silence, the relationships he could not repair, the words he could not forget, and the merciless conviction that everything he suffered revealed some intrinsic defect within himself. Asmodeus needed no executioner. He had taught his captive to become his own.

And in the black scripture of the King's dominion, the following condemnation was inscribed: Worthless in love. Worthless in friendship. Worthless before the household that should have sheltered him. Worthless before the strangers whose acceptance he pursued. Worthless even in his attempts to prove himself worthy. What offering could such a creature bring before the throne? Neither innocence, for it had been defiled by bitterness; nor happiness, for he had scarcely known it; nor dignity, for he had surrendered it a thousand times in pursuit of affection. Only suffering. An immeasurable accumulation of grief, loneliness, longing, humiliation, and hatred, gathered over the course of an existence and presented before the altar of the infernal sovereign. And for the greatness of this suffering alone, the King would permit the offering to be laid at his feet.

Thus spoke the cruelty of Asmodeus. He pronounced deprivation a verdict, suffering a virtue, humiliation a sacrament, and self-hatred the highest form of obedience. He wished his captive to regard every kindness he had ever offered as foolishness, every expression of love as weakness, and every hope of companionship as evidence that he had not yet been sufficiently broken. For the ultimate ambition of the King was not to make him suffer. It was to make him believe that suffering was good, that he deserved every moment of it, and that the cruelty of the world was merely the execution of a judgment passed upon him before his birth.

And when the darkness became so complete that he could no longer distinguish his own despair from the voice of his tormentor, Asmodeus proclaimed his dominion absolute. The King's greatest triumph was the theft of authorship itself. Every cruel thought that entered the man's mind bore the King's invisible signature. Every accusation appeared to arise spontaneously from his own conscience. Every memory of rejection became testimony in a trial where the accused had been persuaded to serve as his own prosecutor. There could be no acquittal within such a court. For Asmodeus had written its laws, selected its witnesses, corrupted its evidence, and forbidden the possibility of mercy.

And so the man stood before the Black Throne, not as a willing disciple, but as one whose suffering had been transformed into a religion. His loneliness was the cathedral. His longing was the incense. His shame was the liturgy. His broken promises were the scripture. His unanswered prayers were the hymns. And his self-hatred was the priest who administered every sacrament. In the innermost sanctuary, where the last remnants of his hope were kept alive only to furnish further torment, the King awaited the completion of his greatest work.

He desired a man who would call himself worthless without being commanded. A man who would remember every rejection and forget every kindness. A man who would worship the memory of what he had lost and despise himself for having wanted it. A man who would mistake his exhaustion for destiny, his isolation for divine judgment, and the voice of his own despair for an eternal law. For the perfect slave of Asmodeus is not he who obeys the King, but he who no longer recognizes the King's commands as anything other than his own thoughts.

And upon the black altar lay the soul of the forsaken man, imagined by its tormentor as a thing already conquered: exhausted, humiliated, starved of tenderness, and desecrated by years of longing. There the King pronounced the final blasphemy of his kingdom: That nothing else had ever been possible. That every hope had been a deception. That every act of love had been an invitation to cruelty. That the lonely man had been fashioned for no purpose beyond his own suffering.

And the most terrible sound in all the infernal dominions was not the laughter of Asmodeus, nor the screaming of his damned, nor the grinding of the great wheel upon which hope was broken. It was the silence of the man, who had heard the condemnation so many times that he could no longer remember when it had first been spoken. Thus stood the dominion of Asmodeus: a kingdom whose darkest miracle was to make its captive believe that the cruelty of his master was indistinguishable from the truth of his own existence.

And in the Book of the Forsaken, beneath the sigil of the Black King, there was written but one terrible commandment:

LET THE SUFFERER BECOME HIS OWN TORMENTOR, AND THE KING SHALL NEVER NEED TO LIFT HIS HAND AGAIN.

In the deepest abyss, beneath the dominions of death and the kingdoms of the damned, sits Asmodeus upon his throne of human misery. He is the Father of Abandonment, the Defiler of Innocence, the Lord of Unrequited Love, and the Eternal King of those whose hearts were fashioned only to be broken. And of all the wretched souls beneath his dominion, none has furnished him with a more enduring monument to suffering than this forsaken man. For Asmodeus was the God of his world. He always had been.

Before he understood the cruelty of men, before he knew the humiliation of rejection, before he could comprehend why affection came so naturally to others and remained so foreign to himself, the Black King had already laid claim to his existence. His childhood was the foundation of the temple. His loneliness was its first sacrament. The absence of tenderness within his own family became the cornerstone upon which the King would erect an empire of despair. The years passed, and he grew into manhood without having known the simple dignity of being chosen. No beloved waited for him. No intimate companion knew the secret chambers of his heart. No faithful friend stood beside him through the long procession of disappointments. He knew the names of countless people, remembered their faces, their words, their promises, and their betrayals, yet remained a stranger to the experience of belonging. And Asmodeus beheld this desolation with unspeakable delight.

For the King understood that the most exquisite cruelty was not to deprive a man of love, but to leave him capable of loving with an intensity that made the deprivation unbearable. Thus was he made both the prisoner and the instrument of his own torment. He wandered among multitudes, entering crowded halls beneath deafening music, seeking in the violence of sound some temporary deliverance from the silence that awaited him. He crossed cities and states, pursued fleeting encounters, and sought human warmth among strangers whose lives continued without him. But wherever he traveled, the King accompanied him. In the crowd, Asmodeus was the distance between him and every other soul. In the silence afterward, he was the realization that nobody had come looking for him. In the unanswered message, he was the slow humiliation of discovering that affection could be offered sincerely and received with indifference.

The King permitted him to hope, for hope was the sharpest of his instruments. He allowed promises to be made and forgotten. He allowed moments of tenderness to bloom beneath the tall pines, where the forsaken man imagined that he had finally glimpsed something beautiful and merciful. He allowed him to believe that perhaps another person might see beyond his suffering and recognize the frightened, longing human being buried beneath it. And when the warmth departed, Asmodeus laughed from his throne. Not the laughter of a beast satisfied by blood, but the immeasurably cruel laughter of a god who had watched a starving man mistake the reflection of bread for nourishment. He delighted in the abasement of the man's desires. What a miserable kingdom, the demon proclaimed, whose subject would surrender every treasure for a single genuine embrace. What a pitiful petitioner, who asks not for power, riches, or dominion, but merely to be remembered when he is absent. Behold the man who would have given everything to be loved, and who has been brought to his knees by the terrible simplicity of that desire.

The King found his greatest amusement in the disparity between the man's intellect and his helplessness. He could dissect the motives of strangers, investigate wrongdoing, recognize deception, and unravel the affairs of others. Yet before the smallest possibility of affection, all his powers seemed to desert him. He could interrogate the world, but he could not compel it to love him. And from this contradiction Asmodeus fashioned the most degrading of his punishments. The man began to hate himself for needing what he could not obtain. He hated the tenderness that made him vulnerable. He hated the hope that survived every humiliation. He hated his own longing, his eagerness, his willingness to forgive, and the pathetic persistence with which his heart returned to the very places where it had been wounded.

The King fed upon this hatred. Every rejection became an accusation. Every accusation became shame. Every shame became self-contempt. And every measure of self-contempt made him approach the world with a greater expectation of cruelty, until even an innocent silence could awaken the memory of every abandonment that had preceded it. Thus did Asmodeus construct the wheel of eternal humiliation. The lonely man sought love. His hunger made him vulnerable. His vulnerability exposed him to disappointment. Disappointment became self-hatred. Self-hatred made intimacy more difficult. And the resulting loneliness drove him again toward the very hunger that had first delivered him into suffering. Around and around the wheel turned, grinding hope into shame and shame into despair, until he could scarcely remember whether he had ever known himself outside its machinery. And the King named this bondage perfection.

For there were no chains upon his wrists, no iron collar around his throat, no walls raised to imprison his body. The chains existed in the memories he could not silence, the relationships he could not repair, the words he could not forget, and the merciless conviction that everything he suffered revealed some intrinsic defect within himself. Asmodeus needed no executioner. He had taught his captive to become his own.

And in the black scripture of the King's dominion, the following condemnation was inscribed: Worthless in love. Worthless in friendship. Worthless before the household that should have sheltered him. Worthless before the strangers whose acceptance he pursued. Worthless even in his attempts to prove himself worthy. What offering could such a creature bring before the throne? Neither innocence, for it had been defiled by bitterness; nor happiness, for he had scarcely known it; nor dignity, for he had surrendered it a thousand times in pursuit of affection. Only suffering. An immeasurable accumulation of grief, loneliness, longing, humiliation, and hatred, gathered over the course of an existence and presented before the altar of the infernal sovereign. And for the greatness of this suffering alone, the King would permit the offering to be laid at his feet.

Thus spoke the cruelty of Asmodeus. He pronounced deprivation a verdict, suffering a virtue, humiliation a sacrament, and self-hatred the highest form of obedience. He wished his captive to regard every kindness he had ever offered as foolishness, every expression of love as weakness, and every hope of companionship as evidence that he had not yet been sufficiently broken. For the ultimate ambition of the King was not to make him suffer. It was to make him believe that suffering was good, that he deserved every moment of it, and that the cruelty of the world was merely the execution of a judgment passed upon him before his birth.

And when the darkness became so complete that he could no longer distinguish his own despair from the voice of his tormentor, Asmodeus proclaimed his dominion absolute. The King's greatest triumph was the theft of authorship itself. Every cruel thought that entered the man's mind bore the King's invisible signature. Every accusation appeared to arise spontaneously from his own conscience. Every memory of rejection became testimony in a trial where the accused had been persuaded to serve as his own prosecutor. There could be no acquittal within such a court. For Asmodeus had written its laws, selected its witnesses, corrupted its evidence, and forbidden the possibility of mercy.

And so the man stood before the Black Throne, not as a willing disciple, but as one whose suffering had been transformed into a religion. His loneliness was the cathedral. His longing was the incense. His shame was the liturgy. His broken promises were the scripture. His unanswered prayers were the hymns. And his self-hatred was the priest who administered every sacrament. In the innermost sanctuary, where the last remnants of his hope were kept alive only to furnish further torment, the King awaited the completion of his greatest work.

He desired a man who would call himself worthless without being commanded. A man who would remember every rejection and forget every kindness. A man who would worship the memory of what he had lost and despise himself for having wanted it. A man who would mistake his exhaustion for destiny, his isolation for divine judgment, and the voice of his own despair for an eternal law. For the perfect slave of Asmodeus is not he who obeys the King, but he who no longer recognizes the King's commands as anything other than his own thoughts.

And upon the black altar lay the soul of the forsaken man, imagined by its tormentor as a thing already conquered: exhausted, humiliated, starved of tenderness, and desecrated by years of longing. There the King pronounced the final blasphemy of his kingdom: That nothing else had ever been possible. That every hope had been a deception. That every act of love had been an invitation to cruelty. That the lonely man had been fashioned for no purpose beyond his own suffering.

And the most terrible sound in all the infernal dominions was not the laughter of Asmodeus, nor the screaming of his damned, nor the grinding of the great wheel upon which hope was broken. It was the silence of the man, who had heard the condemnation so many times that he could no longer remember when it had first been spoken. Thus stood the dominion of Asmodeus: a kingdom whose darkest miracle was to make its captive believe that the cruelty of his master was indistinguishable from the truth of his own existence.

And in the Book of the Forsaken, beneath the sigil of the Black King, there was written but one terrible commandment:

LET THE SUFFERER BECOME HIS OWN TORMENTOR, AND THE KING SHALL NEVER NEED TO LIFT HIS HAND AGAIN.

" Beauseant at Montgisard 1177 "
by Artist Michael Rucker
copyright ©

Description
This painting places a Templar knight at the heart of one of the most improbable victories of the Crusades. On 25 November 1177, sixteen-year-old King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem already marked by leprosy rode out with a few hundred knights to stop Saladins Ayyubid army from reaching the Holy City. With him came Grand Master Eudes de Saint-Amand and roughly eighty Knights Templar from Gaza.

Contemporary estimates give the Christians perhaps 375450 knights and several thousand infantry against a far larger Muslim host that had been allowed to scatter while raiding. Saladin, confident the leper king would stay behind walls, was caught crossing broken ground near Montgisard (Tell Gezer / Mons Gisardi), between Ramla and Yibna. Baldwin knelt before a fragment of the True Cross, then ordered the charge. The Templars formed the spearhead. Their war banner, the Beauseant black above white, black to enemies, white to friends was the signal that no brother might quit the field while it still flew.

The shock of heavy cavalry smashed the unready Ayyubid line. Saladin himself barely escaped; most of his army did not.The scene you see is not a portrait of one named man but an emblem of that hour: white mantle and red cross pattee of the Temple, kite shield, the Beauseant replacing later anachronisms, stone churches of the Latin East rising behind the dust. It is offered so visitors may remember that history is not only catastrophe. Sometimes a small, disciplined force, a young king who would not hide, and a banner that meant we do not leave changed the map for a season.

Baldwins victory bought the Kingdom of Jerusalem nearly a decade. Saladin would return; Hattin and the fall of Jerusalem still lay ahead. Yet Montgisard remains the day the Temples black-and-white standard flew over a field that should have been lost.Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam.

Elon Musk’s journey with SpaceX offers a powerful example of what persistence can achieve. When the company began developing reusable rockets, landing a rocket booster and bringing it safely back to Earth was an extraordinarily difficult challenge.

The early attempts did not succeed. Rockets were lost, lessons were learned, and the work continued. Eventually, SpaceX achieved a successful landing, proving that a difficult goal could become possible through patience, learning, and determination.
The significance is not simply the landing itself. It is the willingness to continue working toward a difficult mission after failure.

Great missions are rarely completed in a single attempt. Sometimes the path forward is built from every mistake, every correction, and every decision to try again.

"The lesson is simple: when the mission has meaning, failure does not have to be the final chapter."

text:
Aaron Lennon was the fastest thing on the pitch. In April 2017 that dream turned into a suffocating nightmare.

A tiny, fearless winger who made Premier League defenders look like they were running in quicksand, he went to two World Cups and played for Tottenham Hotspur and Everton. He lived the dream that millions of kids in England would give anything for. He grew up in a tough part of Leeds and was a phenomenal talent. He became the youngest player in Premier League history at the time when he made his Leeds United debut at just 16. In 2005 he joined Tottenham Hotspur and became a fan favourite at White Hart Lane. His pace was electric. His direct running terrified full-backs. He played 364 games for Spurs and was capped 21 times by England. To the outside world Aaron Lennon had it all — the money, the fame, the career.

Behind closed doors he was fighting a war he was losing. The pressure of professional football is immense: the constant scrutiny, the injuries, the expectation. But Aaron was dealing with more than just football. He was dealing with the weight of severe personal struggles and anxiety that were quietly crushing him. He wore a mask. He smiled in training. He did his media duties. But inside he was falling apart.

By April 2017 he had reached breaking point. On a Sunday afternoon police were called to a busy road in Salford. There were concerns for the welfare of a man. That man was Aaron Lennon. He was detained by police under the Mental Health Act. A Premier League footballer, an England international, was standing on the edge of a busy road in such a state of crisis that the police had to step in to save his life. It was a moment of complete, terrifying vulnerability.

The news broke and the football world was stunned. How could a player who was always so energetic, so fast, so full of life, be suffering so deeply? Aaron later admitted he had been struggling with his mental health for years. He said he was “embarrassed” at first, but he couldn’t hold it in any longer. He took a step away from the game. He went into a treatment centre. He had to learn how to be okay again.

The reaction from the football community was incredible. Everton, his club at the time, offered him their full support. Fans sent him messages of love. Players from across the league stood by him. It gave Aaron the courage to fight back. He recovered. He returned to football. He even played in Turkey before returning to England to finish his career.

But his greatest legacy is not what he did on the pitch. It is what he did after he was detained on that road. He took off the mask. He started speaking openly about his mental health. He wanted other young men to know that it’s okay not to be okay. He wanted to break the stigma that men, especially footballers, have to be tough all the time.

Aaron Lennon proved that the strongest thing a man can do is not run fast or score goals. The strongest thing a man can do is ask for help when he’s drowning. He is a survivor. And he has shown the football world that it’s okay to take off the mask.

text:
Yahweh is the master and his people are his servants.

1. Yahweh identifies Himself as master, not friend

Malachi 1:6

A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear? saith the LORD of hosts unto you...

Yahweh explicitly frames the relationship around master, servant, honor, and fear.

Compare:

John 15:15 — Jesus

Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends...

2. Yahweh demands fear and obedience

Deuteronomy 10:12–13

12 And now, Israel, what doth the LORD thy God require of thee, but to fear the LORD thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the LORD thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul,13 To keep the commandments of the LORD, and his statutes, which I command thee this day for thy good?

Compare:
John 15:14–15 — Jesus

14 Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.15 Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends...

Notice that Jesus still expects obedience, but he describes the relationship as friendship and sharing what he knows from the Father.

3. Yahweh calls Israel His servants

Leviticus 25:55
For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.

Compare:

John 15:15

Henceforth I call you not servants... but I have called you friends...

4. Yahweh describes friendship as an exceptional relationship

Isaiah 41:8

But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.

Notice the distinction: Israel is called God's servant, while Abraham is singled out as God's friend.

2 Chronicles 20:7

Art not thou our God, who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Israel, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?

James 2:23 later repeats this description:

And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

5. Yahweh requires submission to His authority

Jeremiah 7:23

But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.

Compare:

John 17:6–8, where Jesus describes making the Father's name and words known to his disciples.

The most revealing comparison

Yahweh's language

Jesus's language

"They are my servants." — Leviticus 25:55

"I have called you friends." — John 15:15
"If I be a master, where is my fear?" — Malachi 1:6
"There is no fear in love." — 1 John 4:18
"Fear the LORD... and serve him." — Deuteronomy 10:12
"I call you not servants... but friends." — John 15:15
Abraham is singled out as God's friend. — Isaiah 41:8
Jesus offers friendship to his disciples. — John 15:15

One qualification: Yahweh does call Abraham His friend, so it would be inaccurate to claim that Yahweh never describes anyone as a friend. The stronger argument is that the Old Testament repeatedly emphasizes servitude, fear, and obedience, while Jesus explicitly elevates his disciples into friendship and shared knowledge.

 Does Jesus describe people as servants of God, or as children of God?

text:
The US offer of up to $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear programme is likely to strengthen the arguments of those within the Iranian establishment who have long questioned US intelligence claims and the role of IAEA inspections.

Two points are particularly relevant.

- First, the offer could reinforce the view that Washington knows far less about the current state and location of Iran’s nuclear programme than it publicly claims. Alternatively, it could be taken as an indication that Iranian counterintelligence has succeeded in disrupting the networks through which the US and Israel previously gathered information inside the country.

- Second, the timing is particularly significant, as IAEA inspectors no longer have access to Iran’s nuclear sites. More importantly, the US announcement itself explicitly refers to the IAEA’s loss of “continuity of knowledge” regarding Iran’s nuclear programme. This is likely to reinforce suspicions among parts of the Iranian establishment that international inspections also served as a source of intelligence for Western governments.

- In this sense, the US initiative may end up strengthening precisely those voices in Tehran that have long argued against allowing international inspectors back into the country.

#Iran

Luka Dončić is averaging 45 over his last four games. Miami showed why that’s so hard to defend.

45 against Toronto. 42 against Miami. 40 at Sacramento. 53 against Portland. Four Lakers wins, with Dončić averaging 45.0 points, 9.0 rebounds and 7.8 assists. What stands out is how differently those games played out. StatMuse

The scoring math. In the first three games of the streak, Luka hit 20 of 40 threes and 33 of 36 free throws. That’s 93 of his 127 points from those two sources, and roughly 74% true shooting across the three games. The 50% from deep is the hot streak. The free throws are why Sacramento still gave up 40 even though he shot under 50% from the field. StatMuse

The Miami game tells you what happens when teams send two. The Heat trapped him in the opening minute. Luka got the ball out early, the Lakers played four-on-three behind the trap, and the possession produced an open three. He finished with 13 assists and two turnovers, and L.A. had 39 assists as a team. That early pass is what makes the coverage so expensive. The defense commits two players before the Lakers have even started attacking the space behind them. https://t.co/xANgJgHlNW

Portland showed where the Lakers still have work to do. Luka scored seven straight to tie the game in the third, then hit the jumper that restored a six-point lead with 27.7 seconds left. In between, Portland went on a 10–0 run while he rested. Miami offered a glimpse of the solution when Austin Reaves helped hold the lead early in the fourth. The question for L.A. is whether the Reaves-led minutes can consistently produce good shots before Luka has to come back and close.

text:
❤️ A Heart of Thanksgiving
 The Blessings We Almost Overlook
An Original Christian Reflection for To God Be the Glory
 “Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:” — Psalm 103:2 KJV
There is something about the month of November that invites us to slow down and remember the goodness of God.
The trees are surrendering their final leaves, the mornings have grown colder, and thoughts are turning toward Thanksgiving tables, family gatherings, and familiar traditions.
We begin counting the blessings for which we are grateful.
Our homes, our families, our daily bread, and the many ways the Lord has provided for us.
But what about the blessings we almost overlook?
The ones that arrive so quietly that we scarcely recognize them as gifts?
Consider the ordinary morning when you wake to find another day waiting.
There may be dishes in the sink, laundry to fold, errands to run, and responsibilities demanding your attention.
Yet hidden among those ordinary things are blessings.
The sound of a familiar voice.
A handwritten letter tucked inside a drawer.
The comfort of a favorite chair.
A neighbor who remembers to ask how you're doing.
The old Bible resting beside your bed, its pages holding promises that have comforted generations of believers.
Even the privilege of having someone to care for can be a blessing we fail to appreciate until the years have passed.
And what about the people who have quietly enriched our lives?
The Sunday school teacher who patiently explained a Bible lesson.
The elderly gentleman who always greeted everyone at church.
The mother who prayed long after her children had fallen asleep.
The friend who listened when words were difficult to find.
Some of these people may no longer be with us, but the kindness they showed remains part of the story of our lives.
Not every blessing comes wrapped in something we can hold. Some come as memories, lessons, prayers, and love that continues to influence us long after the moment has passed.
There is another blessing we sometimes overlook.
The opportunity to become a blessing to somebody else.
A little encouragement offered at the right moment.
A visit to someone who seldom has company.
A prayer spoken for a friend facing a difficult season.
A few minutes spent listening without watching the clock.
These may seem like small things, but their value cannot always be measured by their size.
And isn't it wonderful that gratitude can be expressed through giving as well as receiving?
When we recognize how generously the Lord has dealt with us, we should desire to extend kindness to others.
Of course, thanksgiving does not mean pretending that every season of life is easy.
Some November tables have an empty chair.
Some hearts are carrying grief.
Some families are facing uncertainty, illness, or burdens known only to themselves and the Lord.
We should never suggest that a thankful Christian must always be cheerful or that sorrow reveals a lack of faith.
The Bible gives us many examples of God's people who experienced deep sorrow while continuing to trust Him.
Thankfulness and tears can dwell within the same faithful heart.
And through every changing season, we have a reason for gratitude that surpasses all earthly blessings.
The wonderful gift of God's Son, Jesus Christ.
Our homes may change. Our circumstances may change. The people around our tables may change as the years go by.
But the Gospel remains the same.
Jesus Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again the third day, according to the Scriptures.
Through faith in Him, we have the promise of eternal life.
No earthly gift can compare with that.
So as Thanksgiving approaches, perhaps we can look beyond the beautiful decorations, the carefully prepared meals, and the traditions we treasure.
Let us remember the ordinary kindnesses, the faithful friendships, the answered prayers, and even the difficult seasons through which the Lord has sustained us.
Let us thank Him for what we have received.
Let us remember those who helped us along the way.
And let us be thoughtful toward those whose Thanksgiving may be quieter or more difficult than our own.
For a heart of thanksgiving is not simply a heart that knows how to count its blessings.
It is a heart that remembers the Giver.
 A Closing Thought
Years from now, we may not remember every dish served at Thanksgiving dinner or every decoration placed upon the table.
But we may remember the hand that reached for ours, the voice that offered a prayer, the laughter shared over a simple meal, or the kindness that made us feel loved.
And perhaps, when we look back, we will discover that some of life's greatest blessings were never the grand occasions we spent so much time preparing for.
They were the quiet gifts of God's goodness, woven so gently into ordinary days that we almost overlooked them.
May we recognize them while they are still ours to enjoy.
And may we never forget to thank the Lord.
 “O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.” — Psalm 107:1 KJV

text:
Zambia's 24-hour-economic fever: Kafue District has stopped sleeping

By Staff Writer 
As darkness settles over Kafue District of Lusaka Province, the lights at Mega Bakery Complex remain on. 
Located on the Lusaka - Livingstone highway, solar-powered streetlights illuminate the frontage, while customers stream into the restaurant, travellers stop for meals and workers keep production moving throughout the night. For a town seeking to reclaim its place as an active commercial and industrial centre, the sight represents more than a business operating beyond conventional hours. It offers a practical demonstration of how private investment, employment creation and government policy can work together to stimulate local economic activity.
At the centre of this transformation is businessman Ilyas Patel, whose Mega Bakery Complex is contributing to efforts to revive Kafue District through a business model built around continuous operations.
Located one of Zambia’s major transport corridors, the one-stop-stocked complex brings together a bakery, restaurant, fast-food café and grocery store. 
Heeding President Hakainde Sammy Hichilema's 24-hour- agenda, Mega Bakery Complex operations have evolved beyond daytime trading, with the entire establishment now running around the clock on three rotating shifts: 08:00 hours to 14:00 hours, 14:00 hours to midnight and midnight to morning.
The result is an enterprise employing more than 80 people, the majority of them women.
Owing to a noted productivity reduction at Kafue Textiles and Nitrogen Chemicals of Zambia (NCZ), any effort increasing employment and incomes is worth commending.
The district's employment opportunities remain an important economic concern, thus any added job and income stream carries a considerable significance. 
Behind every shift are households supported by regular work, from bakers and cooks to waiters, cashiers, cleaners, counter attendants and security personnel. This investment equally demonstrates how businesses can complement government efforts to stimulate economic activity beyond Lusaka and in turn strengthen the productive capacity of all the 116 districts across Zambia's ten provinces; Central, Copperbelt Eastern, Luapula, Lusaka, Muchinga Northern, North-Western, Southern and Western. One of the most visible aspects of Patel’s investment is the installation of solar streetlights  aon a 50-metre stretch in front of the complex.
The lighting has transformed the business frontage into a brightly illuminated commercial space, welcoming to motorists, truck drivers, customers and other travellers who would otherwise encounter poorly lit premises during late-night journeys.
Beyond visibility, speaks to an important requirement of a functioning 24-hour economy: creating an environment where people can work, trade&access services after sunset. The complex has invested in generators, a solar inverter and comprehensive Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) surveillance to support uninterrupted operations and strengthen security.These investments are particularly important in a business environment where power interruptions, security concerns and the cost of operating at night can discourage entrepreneurs from extending their trading hours.Patel believes Kafue has considerable untapped potential. “I have always believed Kafue is a sleeping giant that needs to wake up. The economy does not have to sleep for Zambia to grow," said Patel.Patel's business model aligns with the government's broader ambition to expand economic activity, improve productivity and create employment through the 24-hour- economy initiative.A pharmacy and a barbershop in the district have extended operating hours, an indication that increased night-time activity encourage other businesses to reconsider traditional trading patterns. After sunset, there is now light, employment& a growing reason for travellers to stop. KNZ Television Rainbow Television Zambia Limited Rainbow Newspaper Zambia Limited (RNZL)

text:
I started telling my wife I wanted sex every morning before she left for work because it helped me have a better day.

One night I turned to her and said, “I’ve noticed something. Whenever we have sex in the morning, my whole day feels lighter.”

She laughed. “So?”

“So I want us to do it every morning.”

She sat up. “Every morning?”

“Yes. Every single one.”

“You’re joking.”

I kissed her shoulder. “I’m serious. Why are you looking at me like I just asked you to run a marathon?”

“Baby, do you know what you’re asking?”

“You’re my wife. Who else am I supposed to ask?”

“I thought marriage was supposed to give me some peace.”

I smiled. “This is peace. You’ll leave the house happier and I’ll have a good day.”

“What happens when I’m tired?”

“Then I’ll be very convincing until you change your mind.”

We negotiated. I wanted five mornings a week. She offered two. We landed on four, with weekends off so she could “recover.”

The first few days I was thrilled. I’d wake up, climb on top of her, and remind her of our deal. By the middle of the week she was dragging.

text:
Rhapsody Of Realities Daily Devotional
Pastor Chris Oyakhilome, Ph.D. 
Theme: ✨THE PRICE WAS FULLY PAID✨ 
Date: Saturday 7TH November, 2026. 

Scriptural Ref: Isaiah 53:6
All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all (Isaiah 53:6).

When Jesus hung on the Cross, He wasn't there because of anything He had done. He was there because of us. The Bible says, “...the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all” (Isaiah 53:6). Every sin, every transgression, every act of unrighteousness was laid upon Him. He became the sin-bearer for the whole world.

When that was consummated in the realm of the spirit, something happened that had never happened before: The Father turned His back on Jesus because our sins had been laid on Him. God is so holy that He doesn't look upon sin. Bearing the sins of the world, Jesus cried out, “...My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46).

This was why He prayed in the Garden of Gethsemane, “...if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt” (Matthew 26:39). He never wanted to be separated from the Father, yet He willingly accepted it because of us.

In the mind of divine justice, every one of us was on that Cross. We were in Him in His crucifixion. We were in Him in His death. When He died, we died. In that death, every man paid for his sins: every man who lived before the Cross, everyone who lived at that time, and everyone who would ever be born into this world.

His blood was divine, and it was adequate. You need never pay again for your sins. Years ago, I knew a guy who did something wrong and gave himself seven knocks on the head as punishment. When I asked him why he did it, he simply said, "Because I did something wrong." He didn't understand the Gospel.

Jesus already bore the punishment for sin. No more punishment remains for those who have accepted His sacrifice. Hebrews 10:14 says, “For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified,” and continues in the 26th verse, “…there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins.” Those who reject His sacrifice choose to bear the consequences themselves, but no one could ever pay for sin apart from Christ.

What a glorious Gospel! The price has been paid in full. Walk in the liberty of this truth. Refuse every form of guilt, condemnation, or self-punishment. The Lord Jesus bore your judgment completely, and through His finished work you've been freely justified before the Father. Hallelujah!

CONFESSION:
The Lord Jesus bore my sins and paid the full price for my justification. I rejoice in this glorious truth and live in the liberty of Christ, free from guilt, condemnation, and every consciousness of sin. I walk in the light of my justification, knowing that the price has been paid in full, in Jesus' Name. Amen.

Further Study:
Romans 5:8-11 KJV 
But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. [9] Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. [10] For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. [11] And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.

2 Corinthians 5:21 KJV
For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.

Hebrews 10:11-14 KJV
And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: [12] But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; [13] From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. [14] For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.

1-Year Bible Reading Plan: Hebrews 7 & Jeremiah 50-51

The Beauty of Democracy and the Power of the People's Choice:

In September 2026, at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, Texas, President Donald Trump promised a $5,000 "Trump Dividend" to every adult U.S. citizen, on the condition that Republicans keep control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The promise was clearly meant to sway voters toward the Republican Party, although the White House argued it was a campaign promise.

American voters were not moved. In the November 3, 2026 midterm elections, a "blue wave" swept away the Republican majorities, and Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress.

In Nigeria, the people of Osun State turned out in large numbers in August to vote their conscience. Despite widespread cash inducements from politicians, they rejected the handouts and elected the governor of their choice.

As Nigerians prepare for the general elections beginning January 16, 2027, I encourage every eligible voter to vote for their future and the future of their children, not for cash handouts that offer only short-term gain.
