I really don't know why #WWECrownJewel is even taking place in Riyadh seriously after what has been going on over there in the ongoing conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi Rebels. 
1. The most pressing argument against holding the event in Riyadh was the direct military threat to the city just weeks before the event, a fatal drone and missile attack struck Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport the very airport the WWE roster and staff have relied on to enter and exit the country on multiple occasions. Furthermore just 24 hours before the show, Saudi air defences intercepted two ballistic missiles fired toward the region Riyadh also faces significant security threats and heightened alert levels due to ongoing drone and ballistic missile attacks linked to the conflict with Yemen's Houthi movement and wider regional tensions involving Iran. Plus, multiple top-tier WWE Superstars have been reluctant to travel to the country for the show and reportedly contacted management to state they did not want to be booked for the show out of safety concerns. While WWE officials tried to reassure them that safety was a priority, industry critics noted that lower-card wrestlers and crew members likely felt immense corporate pressure to travel regardless of their comfort level and that WWE had to offer crew members a $3,000 "hazard pay" bonus to incentivise them to make the trip, with a significant portion of the broadcast engineering handled remotely from the US to minimise the number of personnel on the ground, including deciding not to send its primary commentators, Michael Cole and Corey Graves to Saudi Arabia instead they will call the event remotely from WWE Headquarters in Stamford, Connecticut. 
2. Also WWE could have held the event somewhere else instead of holding it in Riyadh like Indianapolis, Indiana or Minneapolis, Minnesota all of which WWE currently have massive, multi-year stadium agreements with both cities. Because Indianapolis (Lucas Oil Stadium) and Minneapolis (U.S. Bank Stadium) are locked into multi-event contracts to host future major premium live events, WWE has direct lines of communication with city officials and stadium management. Pushing an emergency event into one of these pre-partnered indoor venues would have been legally and promotionally smoother than trying to negotiate from scratch elsewhere or as a alternative, analysts have pointed out that the Spectrum Centre in Charlotte, North Carolina currently have a completely clear schedule. Because Charlotte is universally known as the "Queen City," WWE could have seamlessly preserved the "royal" branding, pomp, and circumstance inherently attached to the Crown Jewel name while keeping its staff safe on American soil.
3. Also the US government issued severe travel restrictions on anyone travelling to the country with the U.S. Department of State placing Saudi Arabia under a strict Level 3 Travel Advisory, explicitly citing missile and drone threats from Iranian-supported Houthis targeting civilian infrastructure. And it is not just the US government that has issued severe travel restrictions on anyone travelling to Saudi Arabia both UK and Australian governments have issued restrictions on travel to the country with the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) expanding its alert to advise against all but essential travel to the entire country of Saudi Arabia. The FCDO specifically warned British nationals to completely avoid King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh—the exact hub WWE personnel needed to use—warning that further airport attacks and severe flight disruptions were "very likely" and the Australian government issuing a do not travel order to anyone from Australia who is thinking of flying to Saudi Arabia for the show. The Australian government issued its most severe warning, advising citizens not to travel to Saudi Arabia at all. They officially told citizens to postpone all planned travel, noting that the security situation was highly volatile.
So those are my reasons why I think #WWE should have either moved or postponed #WWECrownJewel from taking place in Riyadh.

text:
I spent much of my time as an Arizona housekeeper making beds in perfect orchestration to Vietnamese girly pop. The Northern Arizona desert is spiritually intense. It’s crawling with demons, lore, suspicion, and unresolved energy. People come to get away from the world, yet find themselves surrounded by others escaping their problems. The labor is hard on your body. Turnover is high. If the isolation doesn’t take you out, seeing yourself through the mirror of others will.

This is where you choose to become who you’re meant to be once and for all. Or return to the shadow world of an inner self never fully offered. The foreigners have a plane ticket home. The Americans have tethers to their past selves.

Making hotel beds is a language. I whip the pillows into the pillowcases, fold the ends and tuck them in with a fluid hand motion. I billow out the fresh, warm sheets as the MIN song pours liquid affection into my ears and courses through my body. The quiet satisfaction as the sheet lands perfectly in the gap behind the mattress. I tuck in the corners with the memorized hand motion and make the final crease for that luxury look. I smooth out the wrinkles as the MIN song reaches its climax. I gently place the pillows diagonally facing the windows. I stretch the ends to make sure they look proud.

“Tuyệt vời biết bao nhiêu, khi có người nuông chiều” (How wonderful it is to be pampered by someone).

Everything has a place. The 8 pillows first get stacked on the chair. 2 coffee K-cups, one decaf, 4 paper cups, 4 plastic cups, 4 condiments, 2 teas. I always found it funny when guests took the K-cups home without using the machine. Yes, it is yours to take, but are you that stingy everywhere else in life too? The Suites had the same products, just in nicer containers. The difference between social class in America is in the packaging. The same buffet breakfast goes on ceramic dishes instead of styrofoam plates. Quite like the McMansions have hollow columns. They’re just building more “air.”

I had an internal code for counting how many towels I needed:

“4, 2, the works” means 4 bath towels, 2 hand towels, 3 washcloths, and a bath mat. If the previous guest didn’t touch the towel origami, they saved me a precious minute.

The Mexican and Ecuadorian housekeepers were the most heartwarming part of the job. They’re cheerful and don’t play mind games. They’re sending remittances back home so they can support their families. How ironic that the “hardest” part of this job, the actual work, is the easiest. The immigrants greet you with a warm smile, and then leave you alone. Stop hiring infertile white cynics and good ol’ boys.

I ate the hotel’s buffet breakfast every morning, and truly enjoyed it. I got excess watermelon for her. So much watermelon that the other guests would comment, “That’s a lot of watermelon, isn’t it?”

A young Indonesian cook tells me he’s lucky to be here. He could expect to make $250 a month back home.

“That’s my girlfriend,” he says about the girl sitting across from him. She’s also Indonesian. They met in America while working as cooks together. They’re both speaking Balinese.

He describes the feeling of seeing the first lights over Los Angeles when his plane landed. The beacon of hope America offers. Many of us don’t see it that way internally anymore.

One day, I’m assigned a housekeeping helper who spends the entire day telling me about meth and jail time in Hawaii. He’s a white American from rural Northern California.

I’m trying to scrub out a tub, so I can get one day closer to Hanoi, and he’s telling me he saw a demon in a forest fire in California? My whole body feels nauseous after that interaction. I wasn’t hungry for dinner. I look into his fiery, wild eyes, his 39-year-old beard with white patches. He says he expunged his demons through finding the Church, but I feel mentally drained receiving all that.

The pain of being an unwitnessed man. He’s an open book. What is coveted about you if you unload yourself on someone you met 20 minutes ago? What is coveted about you if you still define yourself by your past?

That hotel had two tip thieves: the hotel’s housemen. Their job was to strip the used bedsheets and remove the towels before the housekeepers entered the room. If the previous guest left $10 on the nightstand, they would swipe it. What they were doing was illegal. It’s an industry-wide problem for larger hotels. One of them was a sweet Mexican man who greeted me with warm enthusiasm several times a day.

I never reported them, and I thought it would be spiritually impure to entrap them. What if he had a child, and his child was destined to do something important in this life? Is it my role to put humans I’ve never met on a different life path?

Another housekeeper used a guest’s $3 tip to entrap one of them. He took photos of the bills’ serial numbers and later reported the missing $3 to management. The next week, I saw in the group chat that the two housemen were called to the office. The following morning, both housemen left a few bills in the rooms after they had stripped them. By the second morning, no money was in the rooms again.

These two men didn’t break the system. The system was already broken by the permissiveness that allowed them to steal. The guy who entrapped them was later fired, not for reporting the tip thief, but for getting in a bar fight with another coworker.

Whenever I felt close to her, the hotel’s power would cut out. I messaged her 14 time zones away: Was that you in your sleep in Hanoi? I step into the hallway. The emergency lights cast a white glow on the housekeeper carts. The HR person is standing there, quite still. Her presence fills the hallway. Something sinister lives in that moment. An alternate life if I don’t pass through the pinhole to Hanoi.

The first rule of transient labor jobs is to have a clear and intentional plan to move on before the spiritually broken hands pull you into the abyss.

The second rule of transient labor jobs is you protect your energy at all costs. Many sleep with their coworkers and have empty liquor bottles on their nightstands.

Unless you want to meet your future wife housekeeping. People do that. Housekeeper couples are still in the National Park to this day, waiting for their parents to die to get their houses.

Protecting your energy starts with the morning shuttle driver who likes to play mind games. The night before, a white apparition stood outside my window. That demon was cute compared to this man’s energy.

I see a cottontail rabbit cleaning its ears in the first rays of sun. I feel her gentle spirit in its presence.

Then the white van rumbles across the desert floor of this double-wide trailer park, approaching the stop at 6:54 AM. The shuttle driver is here. The rabbit hops away.

Some days, he pretends to swerve at us. Other days, he rolls the vehicle slowly 20 feet past where we’re standing. It’s all plausibly deniable. 100 minor things to create extreme irritation, but nothing major enough to go to HR with.

“Chris wants to get us all killed,” he says one morning after his fake swerve. It’s too slow to be dangerous, but obvious enough to know that the sovereignty of your mind is being tested.

“Good morning, Chrissy Poo, I mean Chris.”

“I used to have spiked hair,” he says to one of the new employees, “Us Idaho boys used to be excited to see the blonde girls at the music festivals in Utah.”

On a hiking trip to the Canyon, a girl with a tube top walks in front of the shuttle van.

“I’ve been married for 20 years, but I’ll still look,” he says. “I could never be with a girl that young. Too much energy.”

You’ll never meet anyone more attention-seeking than old men without children. He’s trying to create lore around himself. He devours those who still have that new employee glow. I learn to sit in the back of the van with my earbuds blasting Vietnamese girly pop.

One day, someone reaches out from my past life on the East Coast. I look to the East past the wide expanse of sagebrush. Dark storm clouds, lightning. I look to the West. Sunshine and rainbows. Vietnam.

Her.

The upcoming airlift from Phoenix airport.

The cute elk told me to book the flight. The same herd of elk who find the hotel’s grass yummy. The street trees are more yummy than the forest trees. When mating season starts in a couple of weeks, they will become aggressive. I pressed the confirm button on the flight exactly as the sun crossed the horizon.

The afternoon shuttle driver is convinced all the hotel staff are involved in human trafficking. He says that hundreds of people disappear from the hotel every year. If he believes what he’s saying, he’s complicit himself. He says he and other old-timers saw lava flowing on one of the old cinder cones. Lava hasn’t flowed in Arizona in 500,000 years. He tells a story that when he was in the Navy, he taught Gaddafi’s son how to play baseball, and he was killed in a US missile strike only a week later. When he’s not on his human trafficking rants, he talks about the water wars in the 1950s with the “cowboys vs. Indians.” His truth preferences are all over the map, as are many unwitnessed men who live in their heads.

“This whole area used to be forest, but the people in California needed firewood. The trees never grew back.”

He wants to buy a parcel of land and put a cabin on it. But one morning, I hear him on the phone asking a supplement company to refund him because it cleaned out his bank account.

The head chef tells me he saw me walking on the road at night. Warns me to carry a big stick, so the coyotes don’t eat me. Or wild boars, or whatever creatures of the night don’t get me first. He’s right about not walking on the road at night in the desert. But not because of the animals. There’s an intense feeling of being watched behind the barbed wire that criss-crosses the desert.

The desert conceals many secrets.

On my first day checking into employee housing, a mom who is a server greets me. She does that annoying “lay of the land” thing, and tells me that most of my housemates are longtime seasonal workers. So that’s how you define yourself?

Her children later fly in to visit her: In employee housing. She says her children visiting made her whole. I can see the pain in her heart to send them off again. How does that mom not have any security?

My first roommate is a 20-year-old dishwasher from Montana. He spends his evenings on the video game stream cursing at the top of his lungs. It’s distressing. I enter the bathroom, and the shower is caked in thick yellow grime several millimeters thick. He has natural soap and shampoo, but I haven’t seen him eat one vegetable. His alarm goes off at 5:30 AM every morning, and he empties his bowels, leaving the door open for the half-digested smell to be my wake-up alarm.

I overheard him on a call with an army recruiter. He says he’s working in a kitchen as a cook, not a dishwasher. The recruiter is excited. He asks him why he doesn’t join the military right now. He replies he wants to work in more National Parks first. But he never goes outside. He’s living on the video game stream. The recruiter’s voice shifts. He knows something doesn’t add up.

The nights are full of apparitions and the sense I’m being watched by a heavy presence. I message her the night I see a white apparition and a scarecrow through the window near another trailer. Vietnam has apparitions too. I turn my head back to the ghost, who is quite still. It looks cute now. I think I’ll go back to sleep.

The one cafe in that truckstop of a town is my refuge to write. Unstained by the unresolved energy of employee housing. The first sips of a matcha latte touch my lips. I watch the dust devils approach the dusty parking lot, and head directly for the front porch. The barista slams the old wooden doors shut just in time. Every few days, boys come in with cowboy hats strapped to their backs.

The smell of sagebrush and dust under a clear blue sky reminds me of camping with my Dad in Nevada in the Summer of 2011. That era is long over. My writing keeps meeting resistance. Am I just milking my soul for money to cross the Pacific? Why am I not offering myself in full capacity?

Maybe none of this is me anymore. None of it at all. Maybe the guilt I’m harboring is no longer mine to bear. Maybe the guilt I’m placing on others for not being there when it mattered was really our paths diverging.

It’s my last day of work. It’s pouring with cloud-to-ground lightning. The wash outside the hotel is flooding. My manager tells us to come to the office urgently. I feel it in my whole body that something is happening. He says a tornado is coming towards the hotel and is 30 minutes away. If it comes, he will pull the fire alarms, and we will take cover behind the front desk.

I go back to making beds. The power flips off and on several times. What is she doing in her sleep?

The tornado doesn’t come, and I cross the street to eat lunch. I send her a message thanking her for stopping the tornado in her sleep.

My very last room has popcorn strewn all over the floor. I have to crawl under the beds with the vacuum cleaner to get it all. The previous guest left behind a small unicorn plushie. When you see that kind of mess, you know it’s from a child, and it warms your heart.

Jose, the Mexican night porter, comes in to wish me farewell before Vietnam. He’s 63 years old and will retire at his home with his family in Mexico City in 3 years. He sees the pink plushie and asks if he can have it to bring to his niece. He thanks me for my “gift,” saying she’ll love it. Then he calls me into another room, where he tells me to take the money left behind by a guest. The tip thieves cleaned these rooms out already. We both know it’s his money.

He hugs me a couple of times. It’s the only hug I got the entire summer. He says I have a great smile, and reminds me to smile more often. It comes from a place of love for my next life. He says to call the front desk and leave a message for him from Vietnam.

The next day, I watched Grand Canyon: Rivers of Time at the IMAX theater. There was one massive takeaway: In 1869, John Powell led the first American expedition to explore the Colorado River through the Canyon. The trip was treacherous. They got capsized many times in rapids and had to constantly recaulk their leaky rowboats. Their food got washed away. Morale was low. Three of their men decided to give up and trek to a settlement 75 miles away. John Powell sent a letter with them to his wife in case the rest of the expedition didn’t make it. Ironically, there was only one rapid left. The three men who quit were never seen again.

It’s funny how the point of quitting is often only a hairline away from when things suddenly start working out. Maybe God is testing how badly we want what we set out for.

My airlift comes much faster than I anticipated.

I watch the Phoenix desert recede from my plane window. That desert took care of me when everyone else released me on a different life path. Maybe it’s time to stop using the word abandon. I expected to see the Phoenix urban sprawl and buttes with relief, but I find myself filled with reverence.

I see the lights of Hanoi as my plane lands 30-something hours later. I think about what that Indonesian boy said about landing in LA for the first time. You’ll never get those moments back. They live in our hearts forever.

She checks my hands at a cafe on West Lake. When I first started my housekeeping job, my hands bled from the friction of the bedsheets. The bleeding stopped once I put moisturizer on them nightly. The smallest acts of love can feel the warmest.

You can’t protect your energy by running or avoiding. The only way is to step through the pinhole. It will break your heart from all the people and outcomes that were once part of you, but it will lead you to offering yourself at your full capacity.

2 Timothy 2:22-23

[22] So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. [23] Have nothing to do with foolish, ignorant controversies; you know that they breed quarrels.

Proverbs 6:16-19

    [16] There are six things that the LORD hates,
        seven that are an abomination to him: 
    [17] haughty eyes, a lying tongue,
        and hands that shed innocent blood, 
    [18] a heart that devises wicked plans,
        feet that make haste to run to evil, 
    [19] a false witness who breathes out lies,
        and one who sows discord among brothers.

In the program of mental belief I commit myself, and abandon all that is not related to that commitment. In personal belief I commit myself morally to this way of confidence and refuse to compromise with any other; and in particular belief I commit myself spiritually to Jesus Christ, and determine in that thing to be dominated by the Lord alone.

2 Timothy 2:24-26

[24] And the Lord’s servant must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone, able to teach, patiently enduring evil, [25] correcting his opponents with gentleness. God may perhaps grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth, [26] and they may come to their senses and escape from the snare of the devil, after being captured by him to do his will.

Psalm 51:16-19

    [16] For you will not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it;
        you will not be pleased with a burnt offering. 
    [17] The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit;
        a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.

    [18] Do good to Zion in your good pleasure;
        build up the walls of Jerusalem; 
    [19] then will you delight in right sacrifices,
        in burnt offerings and whole burnt offerings;
        then bulls will be offered on your altar.

When I stand face to face with Jesus Christ and He says to me — “Believest thou this?” I find that faith is as natural as breathing, and I am staggered that I was so stupid as not to trust Him before.

Psalm 53:6

    [6] Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion!
        When God restores the fortunes of his people,
        let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

text:
Pillar I: The Textual & Historical Exposition (1 Kings 15–18)
1. The Dynastic Instability of the North vs. The Davidic Lamp in Judah (1 Kings 15–16)
The canonical record in chapters 15 and 16 contrasts the preserved Davidic covenant in Jerusalem with the rapid, violent turnover of dynasties in the northern kingdom of Israel.
The Southern Succession (Abijam and Asa): Abijam’s heart was not loyal to the Lord (lō-hāyāh ləbābō šālēm), walking in the sins of Rehoboam. Yet, for David’s sake, God preserved “a lamp in Jerusalem” (1 Kings 15:4). When Asa assumed the throne, he executed substantive domestic and civil reform: removing foreign cults, banishing cult prostitutes, and deposing his grandmother Maachah from her royal status because she erected an obscene image for Asherah (1 Kings 15:11–13). Nevertheless, Asa’s later years revealed the recurring snare of horizontal statecraft: when threatened by Baasha of Israel, Asa raided the temple and royal treasuries to hire Ben-Hadad of Syria as an unholy military confederate, demonstrating how easily covenant leaders default to financial bribery and pragmatic alliances when pressured by physical adversaries (1 Kings 15:18–20).
The Northern Foreclosures (Nadab to Ahab): In the North, the absence of covenant foundation produced relentless civil bloodshed and dynastic collapse. Jeroboam’s house was extinguished by Baasha (1 Kings 15:27–30), fulfilling the Ahijah prophecy. Baasha’s son Elah was assassinated while drunken by Zimri, who reigned only seven days before burning the royal citadel over his own head (1 Kings 16:9–18). From the subsequent civil war between Tibni and Omri emerged the Omride dynasty.
The Omride Synthesis & Ahab’s Escalation (1 Kings 16:25–33): Omri institutionalized commercial statecraft, building Samaria as an economic hub. His son Ahab, however, did evil beyond all who preceded him. Ahab treated the “sin of Jeroboam” (the golden calves at Bethel and Dan) as a light, trivial matter, escalating to full state syncretism by marrying Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, priest-king of the Sidonians. Ahab imported Phoenician Baalism, erected a formal temple and altar to Baal in Samaria, and crafted an Asherah pole, institutionalizing an aggressive, predatory fertility cult designed to replace the statutory worship of Yahweh entirely.
2. The Drought Decree and the Provision of the Sovereign (1 Kings 17)
Into this total collapse of state and religious fidelity stepped Elijah the Tishbite.
The Statutory Injunction (1 Kings 17:1): Elijah stood before Ahab and declared: “As the LORD God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, except at my word.” This was not an arbitrary meteorological display. Under Deuteronomy 11:16–17 and Deuteronomy 28:23–24, drought was the explicit statutory sanction enacted when the nation turned aside to serve other gods. By striking the rain, Yahweh issued a direct judicial strike against Baal, who was venerated across the Levant as the storm god who commanded the clouds, lightning, and agricultural fertility.
The Brook Cherith & The Ravens (1 Kings 17:2–6): Elijah was commanded to hide eastward by the brook Cherith. The prophet was sustained through secondary, non-human means—ravens bringing bread and meat morning and evening, drinking from the wadi until the drying of the waters tested his obedience.
The Widow of Zarephath (1 Kings 17:7–24): When the brook dried, Elijah was commanded to cross directly into Gentile territory—Zarephath of Sidon, the very cultural backyard of Jezebel and her father Ethbaal. The prophet found a destitute widow gathering sticks to prepare a final meal before dying of starvation. Elijah commanded her to bake a cake for him first, testing creaturely trust against divine promise: “The bin of flour shall not be used up, nor shall the jar of oil run dry, until the day the LORD sends rain on the earth” (17:14).
Resurrection in the Upper Chamber: When the widow’s son died, the crisis of mortality breached the domestic sanctuary. Elijah carried the child to the upper room, cried out to Yahweh, and stretched himself upon the boy three times until the soul (nephesh) returned. This confirmed the sovereign jurisdiction of the God of Abraham over life, death, and physical resurrection outside the territorial borders of Israel.
3. The Confrontation on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18)
In the third year of the drought, God commanded Elijah to present himself to Ahab to release the rain.
Obadiah and the Divided Household (1 Kings 18:1–16): The text introduces Obadiah, Ahab’s royal palace steward who “feared the Lord greatly.” While Jezebel systematically massacred the prophets of Yahweh, Obadiah took a hundred prophets, hid them by fifties in caves, and fed them with bread and water. Obadiah embodies the severe tension of the faithful administrator operating within the belly of a tyrannical, apostate regime, balancing logistical preservation with the terror of state exposure.
The Indictment of the Troubler (1 Kings 18:17–19): When Ahab met Elijah, the king uttered the accusation of the compromised magistrate: “Is that you, O troubler of Israel?” Elijah returned the statutory indictment: “I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father’s house have, in that you have forsaken the commandments of the LORD and have followed the Baals.” True covenant disturbance is not the voice that exposes sin, but the leadership that commits the treason.
Carmel: The Plumb Line of Limping (1 Kings 18:20–21): Elijah assembled the nation, the 450 prophets of Baal, and the 400 prophets of Asherah at Mount Carmel. He confronted the populace with their operational compromise: “How long will you falter between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow Him; but if Baal, follow him.” The Hebrew verb for “falter” (pōsaḥîm) denotes limping, hopping, or dancing erratically from one branch to another—a forensic indictment of syncretism. The people answered him not a word; compromise paralyzes the witness.
The Fire Audit (1 Kings 18:22–39): The challenge was binary. Two bulls, two altars, no artificial ignition: “The God who answers by fire, He is God.” The prophets of Baal performed ecstatic rituals, cried from morning till evening, leaped around their altar, and cut themselves with knives according to their ceremonial customs until blood gushed out, yet “there was no voice; no one answered, no one paid attention” (18:29). The mechanical devices and self-mutilation of paganism yielded absolute silence.
Rebuilding the Ruined Altar: In contrast, Elijah took twelve stones representing the twelve tribes of the sons of Jacob—re-establishing the uncompromised unity of the whole covenant community, rejecting the geopolitical schism of the monarchy. He dug a deep trench, arranged the wood, placed the sacrifice, and ordered four waterpots of water to be poured over the altar three consecutive times, saturating the wood and filling the trench to eliminate all human suspicion of hidden fire.
The Prayer and the Cleansing: At the exact hour of the evening sacrifice, Elijah approached and offered a simple, non-theatrical prayer invoking the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. The fire of Yahweh fell, instantly consuming the burnt sacrifice, the wood, the twelve stones, the dust, and licking up the water in the trench. Confronted with unmediated divine majesty, the people fell on their faces, crying: “The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!”
The Execution of the Usurpers: Operating under Torah statutory law governing apostasy and false prophets (Deuteronomy 13:1–5; 18:20), Elijah commanded the seizure of the 450 prophets of Baal, bringing them down to the Brook Kishon to be executed, purging the land of the cartel that had seduced the nation.
The Torrent of Rain (1 Kings 18:41–46): Elijah ascended Carmel, bowed to the earth, and prayed seven times while his servant watched the sea. When a cloud as small as a human hand arose from the water, Elijah warned Ahab to prepare his chariot before the downpour halted him. The hand of Yahweh came upon Elijah, and he girded up his loins and outran Ahab’s royal chariot to the entrance of Jezreel.
Pillar II: Deeper Theological Meanings & Covenant Jurisprudence
The Inviolability of Statutory Retribution (The Drought Mechanism):
The three-and-a-half-year drought was not a spontaneous display of prophetic outrage. In Deuteronomy 28:23–24, God explicitly warned Israel that if they departed from the Law, the heaven over their heads would be bronze and the earth beneath them iron. Elijah’s prayer was an appeal to the divine court to execute the written terms of the covenant ledger. When God withholdeth the rain, He dismantled the theological legitimacy of Baal in the exact sphere of his supposed mastery. God uses the physical breakdown of nature to expose the spiritual impotence of human idols.
The Anatomy of Limping Syncretism (Pesach vs. Pasaḥ):
Elijah’s indictment of the people “limping between two opinions” exposes the perennial strategy of fallen man. Israel did not want to formally abandon the God of Sinai; they simply wanted to add Baal to insure their crop yields in a Canaanite market economy. Scripture permits zero additive syncretism. A mind that attempts to balance biblical truth with worldly consensus is constitutionally fractured. Elijah forced the confrontation to a binary choice: there is no middle ground between the Living God and an artificial construct.
The Restoration of the Ruined Altar of Twelve Stones:
Before fire could fall, the physical geometry of the altar had to be reconstituted. Jeroboam’s civil partition had sundered the nation into ten northern tribes and two southern tribes. Elijah’s deployment of twelve stones affirmed that the covenant people of God remain a singular, undivided organic whole in the eyes of the Lawgiver, regardless of horizontal political fractures. True reformation does not accommodate geopolitical compromises; it rebuilds upon the ancient, unhewn foundations.
The Principle of Total Saturation (The Removal of the Chisel):
By drenching the altar with twelve jars of water in the midst of a catastrophic drought—spending a resource more precious than gold—Elijah systematically eliminated every possible claim of human contrivance, hidden sparks, or creaturely synergy. When the fire of heaven descended, it consumed not only the meat, but the very stones, dust, and water. True divine power works at the exact point where creaturely capacity has been completely exhausted and drenched in physical impossibility.
The Tension of the Under-Rower (Obadiah vs. Elijah):
The interaction between Obadiah and Elijah in Chapter 18 reveals two distinct offices of covenant preservation during an era of institutional apostasy. Elijah is the external prophet: uncompromising, operating outside the administrative grid, and issuing direct statutory decrees against the throne. Obadiah is the internal sentinel: stationed within the lion’s den of Ahab’s palace, using his delegated administrative office to covertly fund, house, and preserve the remnant prophets in the caves. Both offices are accountable to the Sovereign King, yet each operates under distinct risks and operational constraints.
Pillar III: Exemplifying the Truth in the Daily Walk
For the seeker of Truth striving to walk uprightly in a culture marked by institutional compromise and moral relativism, 1 Kings 15–18 provides four unyielding rules of engagement:
Purge the Secondary Altars from Your Own Household (The Asa Protocol):
Reformation must begin opposite one’s own threshold before it can confront the public square. Asa removed the idols of his fathers and had the moral courage to strip his own grandmother of queenly authority because of her private idolatry. If you are harboring cultural idols, compromising entertainment, or unbiblical dependencies within your gates out of sentimental loyalty to family or tradition, execute immediate eviction. Do not negotiate with what God has commanded to be put away.
Cease the Limping of Dual Allegiance:
Examine where your daily actions contradict your professed confession. Are you trusting the Word of God on the Lord’s Day while adopting the manipulative, fear-driven ethics of the corporate and secular matrix throughout the week? Decide the question of jurisdiction once and for all. If the Lord is God, align your business, your calendar, your finances, and your speech with His statutes without hedging your bets against the world.
Rest in Sovereign Provision at Your Appointed Station:
Whether God assigns you to Cherith (the quiet place of isolation and derived provision), to Zarephath (laboring in the midst of a hostile culture with depleted reserves), or into Ahab’s court like Obadiah (quietly guarding the vulnerable from within hostile infrastructure), do not panic over the drying brook. The faithful steward does not hoard in terror; he bakes the cake of obedience first, confident that the barrel of meal and the cruise of oil are sustained by divine decree, not horizontal market conditions.
Stand Unshaken When Labeled the “Troubler”:
When you stand firm on the immutable Word of God, compromised religious leaders, family members, and civil authorities will accuse you of causing division, disrupting peace, and “troubling” the camp. Do not accept their inverted framing. Recognize that those who breach the commandments of God are the true architects of civilizational ruin. Maintain a clear conscience, keep your trowel in one hand and your sword in the other, and let your life demonstrate the unvarnished reality that the Lord, He is God.

text:
Gaza is not “the world’s largest open-air prison.” That framing ignores basic facts and the choices made by Palestinian leadership for decades.
Israel fully withdrew from Gaza in 2005 — every soldier and every settler. Egypt controls the other border. After Hamas seized power in a 2007 coup, it chose to turn Gaza into a launchpad for rockets and tunnels instead of building a functioning society. Billions in aid poured in; a large part went to military infrastructure, leadership luxury, and paying families of attackers rather than electricity, water systems, or jobs.
The real obstacle has been ideological. Palestinian school curricula (used in UNRWA schools) and Hamas children’s media have systematically taught hatred of Jews, glorification of martyrdom, and the rejection of Israel’s existence for generations. Multiple peace offers that would have created a Palestinian state were rejected (1947, Camp David 2000, 2008, etc.). The original Hamas charter was openly antisemitic. This is not the same as ordinary national conflict — it is a doctrine that prioritizes destroying the neighbor over building one’s own society.
Compare this to actual prisons and genuine humanitarian disasters:
•  North Korea is a real open-air prison. Citizens cannot leave. The regime runs total control, concentration camps, and engineered famine. No one calls it “resistance.” It is pure totalitarian rule.
•  In sub-Saharan Africa, hundreds of thousands of children die every year from malnutrition and related diseases (roughly 600,000 linked to growth failure in recent estimates). These are tragedies of poverty, poor governance, and weak institutions. They are not turned into a global political cause that demands the destruction of a neighboring country, nor are the deaths framed as the fault of an external “occupier” while the local leadership is excused.
Palestinians have had opportunities for statehood and economic development that many poorer populations never received. The persistent refusal to accept any arrangement that leaves a Jewish state standing, combined with an education system that raises children on martyrdom and antisemitism, is the main reason the situation has not improved in nearly 80 years. Leadership choices, not an inescapable “prison,” explain the outcome.

#OTD in 2013, I released the official preview of my debut full-length studio album, "The Art of Céran." The album was actually released commercially earlier that year in 2013 on February 5, 2013, and accrued sales stateside and in Germany and thousands of streams in those aforementioned markets as well as in Brazil, Canada, India, Indonesia, Japan, and Mexico.

The album actually saw its initial release on a limited scale to critics on September 4, 2012, and the album received a 3.5 star rating (out of 5) from Omro Town, Wisconsin-based music critic, Matthew Forss. Additional positive testimonials from Mount Vernon, New York's Jason Randall Smith, New Orleans, Louisiana's Nick DeRiso, and Zebulon, North Carolina's Kelly O'Neil also subsequently ensued. 

"The Art of Céran" was actually REALLY GOOD, and I just ADORE taking a trip down memory lane and listening to it! I was just a teenager when I recorded it (I'll be a middle-aged man in late April), and it's still so very special, because it's where it ALL began, and remains my very first record!

“Born and raised in Kansas City, Missouri, Carlton DuBois McClain fell in love with the arts at an early age. Judging from his bio, his life has been immersed in a nonstop series of theater productions, talent shows, visual art explorations and piano lessons. A classically trained musician, he would eventually marry music with poetry, giving birth to a budding singer and songwriter that would take on the stage name Céran. “The Art of Céran” is his debut album, an ambitious project that crosses a myriad of influences ranging from Latin numbers and love ballads to R&B and pop singles...Despite Céran’s extensive study in music theory, he is clearly open to various styles of popular music. “Love You For Who You Are” is driven by an infectious break, dominant piano chords and male pop group vocal harmonies that nod towards Motown.”

~Jason Randall Smith of Mount Vernon, NY (Review You CD Reviews)

“The soaring ballad “Why Can’t I Live In Your Heart” explores a series of darkly ruminative thoughts on moving past loss – very much in the style of Stevie Wonder...“Axiom” rights things, as the Kansas City native explores the turbulent atmosphere of Seal’s best work, and with a similarly engaging vocal style. “The Hands of Time…” has, at its core, the billowing power of a heart-filled gospel song, pointing to Céran’s earliest days performing in the church. His take on the Dean Martin classic ["You're Nobody Till Somebody Loves You"] is a slow-cooked triumph, too, highlighted by a twilit piano accompaniment..."The Art of Céran" then concludes with a similarly impactful pairing of keyboard-driven ballads. “Nothing But a Memory” has a pleasingly retro feel, from its opening statement on the electric piano through to its direct, almost confidential lyric. It’s another showcase for the impressive dynamic range that Céran possesses, as he aims this time for an unsentimental romantic toughness..."All That You Want Me to Be” ends “The Art of Céran” on an appropriately anthematic note, as Céran offers a series of caressingly beautiful insinuations – all without ever losing his grip on the song's broader theme."

~Nick DeRiso of New Orleans, LA (Review You CD Reviews)

“Jumping back to the '80s dance sound is “This Last Dance” which could be a tribute to producer Narada Michael Walden’s work with Whitney Houston. The modulation is tasteful and vibe is fun with the easy repetitive accent on the second and third downbeats.”

~Kelly O'Neil of Zebulon, NC (Review You CD Reviews)

🇾🇪|Sana’a’s Supreme Political Council Names the Massacre and Files It. The Same Day, a Tanker Is Hit 16 Nautical Miles East of Khasab.

The Supreme Political Council’s Statement Is a Legal Document, Not a Condemnation

The Supreme Political Council — the highest political authority in Sana’a — issued its position on the Al-Hadara market massacre in Al-Waziyah district, Taiz.

The operative clauses:

◾It holds the Saudi regime fully responsible for the massacre and for its legal and humanitarian consequences.
◾It states that targeting civilians, markets and civilian facilities, and violating the sovereignty of Yemen will not go unpunished.
◾ It affirms Yemen will exercise its legitimate right to defend its people and its sovereignty.
◾ It calls on the United Nations, the Security Council, and international and human rights organisations to break what it calls their shameful silence.
◾ It instructs the government and relevant authorities to assess the damage, document the evidence, and complete the necessary legal and human rights procedures.
◾It declares that the blood of the Yemeni people will not be subject to statute of limitations.

That last clause is the one to read twice. A political body does not invoke a statute of limitations unless it intends to build a case file. The Council is not issuing a statement for the news cycle. It is opening a docket, with instructions to document, assess and preserve evidence.

This is the same instrument the Iranian judiciary has been running: 159 indictments against US and Israeli officials over the assassination of Imam Ali Khamenei, verdicts exceeding $290 billion against the United States, a $48 billion Soleimani judgment in the execution phase, and the Minab school file lodged at the United Nations and classified as a war crime.

Sana’a has now placed the Taiz market on the same track. The Council named the responsible party, the evidence procedure, and the principle that the crime does not expire.

The Massacre Itself

Al-Hadara market, Al-Waziyah district, western Taiz. Struck by Saudi-led coalition aircraft at the peak of its weekly trading hours.

The Yemeni Ministry of Health reports 30 deaths and dozens of injured. The Political Bureau of Ansar Allah had earlier put the toll at more than 30 martyrs and wounded. The count rose as the bodies were recovered.

Thirty names were released:

Ibrahim Al-Wasi. Ahmed Salem Saqio. Ahmed Mahboub. Ahmed Khair. Adam Al-Muqati. Abu Al-Jannat Al-Muqati. Islam Al-Alwan Al-Zughair. Burhan Al-Wasi. Bekr Mohammed Ghanim. Tawfiq Talbush. Khalid Mohammed Thabit. Saddam Ahmed. Adel Al-Oshaqi. Arif Ahmed Khair. Abdul Salam Mohammed Abdullah Al-Qais. Abdul Wali Salem Hashid. Abdu Hassan Al-Abyad. Abdu Awad Al-Hadali. Ghasham Al-Hamruri. Fouad Abdu Saeed. Fouad Abdullah Al-Wasi. Mahboub Saleh Tawiro. Mohammed Idris Al-Kazimi. Mohammed Ahmed Abdu Hilal. Mustafa Al-Alwan Saeed. Mahboub Ghaleb Al-Mersa, a resident of Al-Qubaita known as “Al-Hukuma.” And the remainder of the list.

The Taiz correspondent Samir Al-Matarib described the scene: corpses and body parts, an unprecedented crime in three months. He reported the market was hit by artillery as well as aircraft, a ground-based weapon fired from positions close enough to Al-Waziyah to range the district.

Saudi Arabia has offered no comment on the names.

The Aircraft, the Bases, the Suppliers

The strikes were flown by F-15 and Typhoon aircraft from Khamis Mushait (18.30°N 42.80°E) and Taif (21.48°N 40.54°E), with missile fire from Najran (17.49°N 44.13°E).

F-15, Boeing, St. Louis, Missouri. The Saudi F-15SA variant sold under a $29.4 billion deal in 2010. American airframes, American maintainers.

Typhoon, BAE Systems, United Kingdom, with Airbus and Leonardo. The Saudi Typhoon contract signed in 2007 is worth £4.4 billion for 72 aircraft. British airframes, British engineers servicing them under the Al Yamamah and Salam arrangements.

The bombs that killed the shoppers in Al-Hadara were carried by American and British aircraft, serviced by American and British hands, launched from Saudi bases.

The Officers Whose Orders Produced the Strike

The Yemeni armed forces published this command structure with names, photographs, bases and locations:

◾ Fahd bin Hamad Al Salman, all Joint Forces in Yemen.
◾ Ali Ayed bin Ali Mutar Al Harithi, Support and Reinforcement Force.
◾ Abdullah bin Fahd Al Sahli Sharurah Force, which manages the operational bases inside Yemen. His headquarters at Sharurah (17.47°N 47.11°E) required a civil defence alert on 5 November.
◾ Bader bin Saleh Al Harbi (Al Ajili), formerly Al Nasr Camp, Aden. Expelled from the Kahub range east of Bab al-Mandab.
◾ Saad bin Muhammad Fnais Al Qahtani, the Al-Mukha and Jabal Al Nar base, relocated to Aden.
◾ Msahel bin Eid Al Otaibi, Mara Camp, Shabwa.
◾ Fares Al-Shammari (Abu Sultan), Marib base. Units expelled east of Al-Jawf.
◾ Zafer Hazam Al Shahrani, Al Mahra.
◾ Muhammad Talal Al Balawi, Hadramaut.
◾ Saeed Al Gamdi, Joint Task Force 808, Socotra.

Jaser Zain Al-Zariqi was captured in Al-Baha.

The Silence the Council Named

The Security Council has never passed a binding resolution holding the Saudi-led coalition accountable for airstrikes on Yemeni civilians. The United States holds the veto that would block one.

The cumulative total since the escalation began stands at 4,197 airstrikes and missile attacks, per Brigadier General Yahya Saree, spokesperson for the Yemeni Armed Forces. 61 in a single 24-hour period, across Sanaa, Al-Jawf, Taiz, Saada, Marib, Lahj, Al-Dhale, Ibb, Hodeidah and Hajjah.

The target list this week alone: a market in Al-Waziyah, a market in Al-Hadara, a water supply project in Al-Sanaa, Al-Shamayteen district, ten airstrikes in Al-Mudharabah, Lahj, farmers and then the paramedics who came for them in Al-Talh, Sahar district, Saada, the home of Sheikh Mansour Sinan in Barah, Maqbana, a technical and vocational training centre in Al-Ma’afer, a mosque in Jaashaa, Hayfan, a factory in Al-Taiziyah, an oil company station in Bajil, Hodeidah, and the empty Al-Jawf desert five times in a day.

The Council’s charge is that the UN has buried the file. The record supports the charge: 4,197 strikes and no binding resolution.

The Strait: A Tanker Hit 16 Nautical Miles East of Khasab

UKMTO reported an incident 16 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman.

The master of an oil tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz outbound reported an explosion at the waterline on the starboard side. The crew are safe. The vessel is under its own power and continuing its voyage.

Locate it. Khasab sits at 26.19°N 56.25°E, on the Musandam peninsula, the Omani territory that forms the southern jaw of the strait. Sixteen nautical miles east places the vessel in the outbound lane of the eastern strait, in the water adjacent to Omani territory.

The Zones Are Multiplying

Count the maritime incidents across this week alone:

▪️ Four tankers mined in a single IRGC communiqué, with two more stopped.
▪️ Three tankers struck by explosions and fire since a single dawn.
▪️ A tanker hit by two projectiles about 14 nautical miles northeast of Lima (26.38°N 56.47°E), with the engine room struck and the Company Security Officer injured.
▪️ A tanker struck approximately 50 nautical miles north of Al-Shamal, Qatar (26.12°N 51.22°E) two missiles or drones, damage reported.
▪️ Two explosions reported in the Strait of Hormuz.
· A vessel struck by an unidentified projectile 9 nautical miles northeast of Lima.
▪️ Now an explosion at the waterline 16 nautical miles east of Khasab, outbound.

Four distinct zones in one week: the eastern strait off Musandam, the southern approach off Lima, the central Gulf north of Qatar, and the outbound lane east of Khasab.

The enforcement regime is not confined to a single line. It is running across the width of the chokepoint and out into the Gulf.

The Legal Frame Is Now Stated by the Navy Itself

The Iranian Army Navy stated that disregard for maritime warnings and entering restricted maritime zones without prior coordination were among the causes of the fires aboard two tankers.

The IRGC Navy published its procedure: approved routes only, transponders kept active, vessels that deviate subject to interception, mining and destruction.

The tanker east of Khasab was outbound, under its own power, with its crew safe. It reported the strike. That is the vessel that followed the reporting procedure. The vessels that did not are the ones that burned.

The Bill

Al-Hadara market, Al-Waziyah, Taiz. Thirty named dead. Dozens wounded. Corpses and body parts, per Samir Al-Matarib. Artillery and aircraft in the same district.

The Supreme Political Council has held the Saudi regime fully responsible, called the UN silence shameful, ordered the evidence documented, and declared the crime does not expire.

4,197 airstrikes. 61 in 24 hours. A market, a water project, medics, a mosque, a factory, a fuel station, and the empty desert.

F-15s from Boeing. Typhoons from BAE Systems. Khamis Mushait, Taif, Najran.

A tanker struck 16 nautical miles east of Khasab, outbound, waterline, starboard, crew safe, still under power. Four maritime zones in a week. The strait opens on terms Tehran has published and Washington has not accepted.

The Council filed the massacre. The tanker filed the enforcement. Both are on the record.

text:
Comparing Accra and Kigali offers a fascinating look at two entirely different urban philosophies in Africa. While both cities serve as major economic and cultural anchors in their respective regions, they approach development through contrasting lenses.

1. City Planning
Kigali (Rating: 9/10): Kigali is widely considered a benchmark for structured urban planning in East Africa. Guided by strict master plans, zoning laws, and proactive government oversight, the city enforces orderly real estate development, designated commercial zones, and managed expansion. While it faces challenges with steep topography and growing housing demands, its infrastructural layout is tightly controlled.
Accra (Rating: 5/10): Accra evolved more organically. It operates as a vibrant, decentralized metropolis driven heavily by private enterprise and informal commerce. This decentralized nature gives it immense cultural energy, but it also results in severe traffic congestion, unplanned sprawl, and infrastructure that often struggles to keep pace with rapid population growth.

2. Beauty & Aesthetics
Kigali (Rating: 8/10): Set across undulating hills, Kigali is celebrated for its immaculate cleanliness, manicured green spaces, and sweeping vantage points. The strict prohibition of non-biodegradable plastic bags and widespread community landscaping give the cityscape a pristine, orderly visual identity.
Accra (Rating: 6/10): Accra’s beauty is raw, coastal, and atmospheric. It features Atlantic ocean views, lively palm-lined beaches, and an eclectic architectural mix ranging from colonial-era landmarks to modern glass builds. Its aesthetic is defined more by its dynamic street life, art scenes, and cultural warmth than clinical neatness.

3. Safety
Kigali (Rating: 9/10): Statistically and experientially, Kigali ranks among the safest cities on the continent. Violent crime rates are very low, street harassment is minimal, and residents and travelers enjoy a high degree of personal security day and night.
Accra (Rating: 6.5/10): Accra is generally safe by regional standards and boasts a deeply welcoming local population, but it requires a higher baseline of vigilance. Petty theft, opportunistic scams, and traffic hazards require locals and visitors to remain alert, particularly in crowded commercial districts or busy nightlife zones.

4. Sustainability
Kigali (Rating: 8.5/10): Rwanda’s capital leads in institutionalized environmental policies. Initiatives like Umuganda (the mandatory monthly community service day focused on cleaning and infrastructure building), strict plastic bans, and strong national pushes toward green energy and reforestation make sustainability a core part of daily civic life.
Accra (Rating: 5.5/10): Sustainability in Accra is heavily spearheaded by grassroots recycling innovators, tech-driven waste management startups, and civil society groups. While municipal authorities face uphill battles with plastic waste management and sanitation infrastructure, creative local circular-economy projects are rapidly scaling up.

Which of these four pillars: planning, aesthetics, safety, or environmental initiatives carries the most weight when you evaluate an urban environment?

$ARM KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM ARM HOLDINGS’ FISCAL Q2 2027 EARNINGS CALL

Arm’s November 4, 2026 earnings call supports a selective rather than indiscriminate expansion of the AI investment thesis. The strongest implications are sustained demand for server CPUs and memory, accelerating substitution of proprietary Arm-based processors for merchant x86 products, and continued spending on semiconductor design infrastructure. The principal negative transmission is that scarce components and higher memory prices are increasing costs elsewhere in the technology supply chain, particularly in smartphones. Arm’s 50% licensing growth should not be interpreted as broad electronics demand growth: actual royalties increased only 8% to $670 million, while edge AI royalties were approximately flat. Its increased confidence in up to $2 billion of cumulative AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 principally reflects improving supply coverage, with commercial deliveries still targeted for January through March 2027. The implications below distinguish company-specific economic exposure from thematic association and separate new information from corroboration of peer results already released. Magnitude refers to business impact, not a predicted share-price move. Country labels identify the principal listing market.

DATA-CENTER PROCESSORS

X86 LOSSES ARE EXTENDING INTO AI HOST PROCESSORS, BUT CPU DEMAND REMAINS STRONG (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected companies: Intel (INTC: United States); Advanced Micro Devices (AMD: United States).

Direction and magnitude: Structurally negative for merchant x86 market share and bargaining power, with greater direct franchise risk for Intel. Moderate negative competitive implications for AMD’s EPYC business, offset by expanding CPU demand and its accelerator franchise. The call does not establish an immediate revenue contraction for either company.

The critical commentary was management’s identification of a transition “away from x86” for the host CPUs connected to accelerators. Arm specifically cited NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform and Google’s transition to Axion alongside TPU version 8. This matters because accelerator deployments have historically created an associated market for merchant host processors. When the accelerator platform incorporates an internally designed Arm CPU, that host-processor opportunity migrates away from Intel or AMD even if total AI infrastructure spending increases.

Arm also expects its share at top hyperscalers to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026, compared with more than 50% in 2025. This is a selected hyperscaler metric, not global server revenue share or installed-base penetration. Nevertheless, the transmission mechanism is clear: additional workloads move onto internally controlled processor platforms, reducing the addressable merchant CPU opportunity and increasing customers’ leverage in price and roadmap negotiations. Intel’s foundry ambitions provide potential exposure to Arm-based designs, but no evidence in this call establishes that lost Xeon economics would be recaptured through foundry contracts.

The important counterweight is market growth. AMD’s November 3 release reported data-center revenue growth of 97%, while Intel’s October 29 release reported data-center and AI revenue growth of 78%. Those figures are not directly comparable CPU-only measures, but they demonstrate that architecture-share pressure can coexist with substantial absolute growth. Arm’s call therefore strengthens a longer-duration market-share concern more than a near-term outright short thesis.

Near-term catalysts are Q4 shipment execution, supply availability and subsequent customer platform announcements. The more consequential fundamental shift is the 2027 to 2029 migration of AI host processing and general-purpose workloads. Arm’s benchmark against AMD EPYC 9755 does not establish superiority over Venice, which management acknowledged was not the comparison product.

NVIDIA CAN CAPTURE MORE CPU CONTENT AS AI SYSTEMS BECOME MORE CPU-INTENSIVE (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected company: NVIDIA (NVDA: United States).

Direction and magnitude: Positive, with moderate strategic significance for platform revenue capture and customer retention. The call provides demand confirmation rather than sufficient evidence for a discrete near-term earnings increase.

Arm identified NVIDIA as a rapidly growing contributor to data-center royalties and highlighted Vera CPUs already offered through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Management also described the CPU’s expanding role in persistent agentic workloads. For NVIDIA, this is not simply evidence that spending is shifting away from GPUs toward an unrelated component category. NVIDIA increasingly supplies both the accelerator and the Arm-based host CPU within its platform.

The transmission mechanism is greater content capture and system-level coordination. NVIDIA can optimize host processing, memory movement and accelerator scheduling together, potentially improving utilization of expensive GPUs while retaining more of the system’s semiconductor value. If CPU requirements rise relative to accelerator requirements, NVIDIA is better positioned than a GPU-only supplier to participate in that spending. Arm’s royalty growth also provides an independent indication that partner-designed CPUs are moving through production, rather than remaining roadmap announcements.

Arm’s own AGI CPU introduces additional competition for standalone CPU workloads. That should not be ignored, but neither should it be confused with direct displacement of NVIDIA’s accelerated-computing platform. The call does not establish substitution away from NVIDIA GPUs, and adoption of an Arm CPU elsewhere in a data center does not determine the accelerator vendor.

The near-term trading checkpoint is NVIDIA’s scheduled November 17 fiscal Q3 results, particularly commentary on Vera, platform supply and deployment conversion. The longer-duration catalyst is calendar 2027 production growth and evidence that CPU, accelerator and infrastructure integration supports higher platform value rather than merely increasing system complexity.

MEMORY AND MOBILE SEMICONDUCTORS

THE MEMORY READ-THROUGH EXTENDS BEYOND HBM INTO SERVER DRAM AND PRICING POWER (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected companies: Micron Technology (MU: United States); SK hynix (000660: South Korea); Samsung Electronics (005930: South Korea).

Direction and magnitude: Positive for server-memory demand and pricing durability. Potentially material at the memory-business level for Micron and SK hynix. Positive for Samsung’s memory operations, with a more mixed consolidated effect because its downstream businesses also bear higher component costs.

Arm repeatedly identified memory as a supply constraint and a major contributor to higher system costs. Rene Haas named Micron, Samsung and SK hynix among the companies with which Arm has longstanding relationships. At the same time, management expects materially higher CPU core counts and sustained growth in agentic workloads.

The transmission mechanism is broader than accelerator HBM demand. More persistent CPU workloads require memory capacity and bandwidth for application state, tool execution, retrieval and orchestration. Higher core counts create additional pressure to provision enough memory resources to keep those cores productive. The strongest product-level implication is therefore support for server DRAM, including DDR5, rather than an automatic inference that every new Arm CPU produces an HBM order.

The pricing signal is particularly important. Arm is discussing cost pass-through rather than expecting rapid normalization in memory procurement costs. Its separate observation that memory prices are depressing smartphone demand shows that upstream scarcity is affecting multiple end markets. This supports a relative preference for scarce-component producers over downstream vendors that cannot fully pass through higher bills of materials.

The suppliers’ own recent disclosures corroborate the mechanism. SK hynix reported significant growth in server DDR5 sales, while Samsung described strong server demand supporting memory prices across applications. These are already disclosed conditions, not newly discovered upside from Arm’s call.

Near-term catalysts are contract-pricing updates, shipment allocation and customer cost-pass-through commentary over the next several quarters. The longer-duration issue is whether rising server-memory requirements remain ahead of qualified supply during 2027. The call does not disclose supplier allocations, purchase values or memory configurations, so it does not support assigning a specific AGI CPU revenue contribution to any vendor.

ARM’S ROYALTY RESILIENCE DOES NOT SIGNAL A SMARTPHONE RECOVERY (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected companies: Qualcomm (QCOM: United States); MediaTek (2454: Taiwan).

Direction and magnitude: Negative for handset-related volumes and near-term margin recovery. Material to the affected businesses, but insufficient to establish a negative consolidated outlook for either company because both have expanding non-handset exposures.

Arm reported approximately flat edge AI royalties, with higher royalty rates offsetting weaker smartphone units. Management stated that higher memory prices continued to pressure smartphones, particularly lower and mid-tier products. This is a direct warning against using stable Arm royalties as evidence that handset shipments or handset semiconductor demand have stabilized.

The economic mechanisms differ across the supply chain. Arm can receive more royalty revenue per chip through richer technology adoption, while a handset chip supplier still faces lower customer production, higher manufacturing costs and greater resistance to processor pricing. A smartphone manufacturer facing a more expensive memory configuration can respond by raising retail prices, reducing specifications, lowering other component budgets or cutting production. Each response can pressure the application-processor supplier through volumes, mix or negotiations.

Qualcomm’s November 4 release provides contemporaneous confirmation: QCT handset revenue declined 26% to $5.137 billion. Qualcomm also described broad input-cost inflation and indicated that the full benefit of pricing actions should reach QCT gross margins in the 2nd half of fiscal 2027. Arm’s commentary therefore reinforces an already reported problem and argues against assuming an immediate margin recovery.

MediaTek’s handset exposure is similarly affected, particularly where device affordability constrains pricing. However, its expanding AI and edge businesses limit the validity of a blanket company-level negative conclusion. The appropriate read-through is to handset assumptions, not an automatic short of the entire company.

Near-term catalysts are handset customer production plans, holiday-season sell-through and evidence that processor price increases are being accepted. The longer-duration recovery depends on device affordability and component availability. Arm’s expectation of a roughly flat smartphone market next year is not protection against another volume decline: its anticipated royalty growth relies partly on monetization improvements that do not transfer directly to Qualcomm or MediaTek.

FOUNDRIES AND SEMICONDUCTOR DESIGN INFRASTRUCTURE

TSMC BENEFITS FROM CPU ARCHITECTURE COMPETITION WITHOUT NEEDING A SINGLE DESIGN WINNER (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected company: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (2330: Taiwan).

Direction and magnitude: Positive for advanced-node manufacturing demand and customer commitment quality. The incremental Arm AGI CPU program is likely modest relative to TSMC’s total business, but the broader architecture shift is strategically supportive.

Arm attributed its improved confidence in up to $2 billion of cumulative silicon revenue partly to additional supply arrangements. It explicitly discussed wafer supply alongside substrates, testing and memory. The manufacturing relationship is verified: TSMC’s statement accompanying the original AGI CPU launch identified it as the manufacturer using its 3nm process.

The direct mechanism is conversion of Arm’s customer commitments into leading-edge wafer demand. The broader mechanism is architecture diversification among TSMC’s customers. A hyperscaler-designed Arm CPU, an Arm merchant CPU and a competing fabless processor can all require advanced manufacturing. TSMC can therefore participate in processor competition without depending on which CPU vendor captures the highest product margin.

The accompanying Arm filing also illustrates how scarce manufacturing capacity changes risk allocation. A capacity agreement covering 2027 through 2029 requires minimum purchases, potential shortfall payments and $200 million of expected advances during the 1st half of calendar 2027, with pricing negotiated quarterly. Such arrangements can shift funding and utilization risk toward the chip designer. However, that agreement’s supplier was not named, so the advance cannot be assigned to TSMC.

Several boundaries prevent overstatement. Arm’s $2 billion opportunity is finished-chip revenue across multiple fiscal years, not TSMC wafer revenue. Some Arm shipments could replace processors already manufactured by TSMC, limiting net incremental wafer demand. The call also does not establish a specific advanced-packaging allocation or new semiconductor-equipment order.

Near-term catalysts are Arm’s fiscal Q3 supply update and commercial shipments in January through March 2027. The longer-duration positive is sustained investment in multiple advanced CPU designs and firmer customer capacity commitments, rather than an assumption that all Arm revenue is incremental to TSMC’s market.

DESIGN TOOLS CAN MONETIZE THE INVESTMENT CYCLE BEFORE PRODUCTION ROYALTIES RECOVER (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected company: Synopsys (SNPS: United States).

Direction and magnitude: Positive for design, verification and interface-IP demand. Moderate significance to the relevant product franchises; the incremental contribution from Arm alone is undisclosed and should not be treated as a consolidated earnings catalyst of known size.

Arm’s licensing revenue increased 50%, and management stated that the need for additional licenses, product variations and technologies “is not slowing down at all.” The company signed 4 additional compute subsystem agreements and described royalties from new designs arriving approximately 12 to 24 months later.

That timing distinction favors suppliers monetizing semiconductor development before volume production. More CPU variants, higher core counts, complex memory interfaces and tighter power constraints increase implementation, verification and system-validation work. Design-tool spending can therefore remain strong even when smartphone units or near-term aggregate royalties are weak.

The Synopsys relationship is not inferred from industry exposure alone. Its March announcement identified specific design, interface-IP, emulation and prototyping products used in the development and verification of Arm AGI CPU. This establishes a direct channel through which Arm’s silicon roadmap and a broader population of Arm-based designs can support demand.

Arm’s intention to perform more work internally does not automatically eliminate this opportunity. Internalizing chip-development tasks can reduce reliance on outside design-service partners while preserving or increasing demand for the tools and interface IP used by Arm’s own engineers. The call does not identify which external partner functions would be reduced, so no specific design-services vendor should be labeled a loser.

The near-term catalyst is evidence of stronger design commitments and hardware-assisted verification demand in subsequent Synopsys disclosures. The longer-duration benefit is continued design complexity across 2027 and later product generations. Arm’s 50% licensing growth should not be transferred directly into a Synopsys growth forecast, particularly because Arm’s ACV increased a more moderate 12%.

CLOUD PLATFORMS AND INFRASTRUCTURE OPERATORS

CUSTOM CPUS STRENGTHEN HYPERSCALER COST CONTROL AND BARGAINING POWER (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected companies: https://t.co/SpqvHNUxpK (AMZN: United States); Alphabet (GOOGL: United States); Microsoft (MSFT: United States).

Direction and magnitude: Positive for infrastructure economics and strategic flexibility. Potentially material within cloud compute operations over time, but a more moderate and unquantified consolidated earnings effect.

Arm identified Amazon, Google and Microsoft as its largest data-center royalty contributors and cited Graviton, Axion and Cobalt as major deployment drivers. Management emphasized that customers designing their own systems can optimize data movement and decide which functions belong in the CPU, networking processor or storage subsystem. That is a more economically meaningful advantage than a generic claim that an Arm core is more efficient.

The transmission mechanism is control over the system cost structure. Custom processors can remove part of the merchant CPU supplier’s margin, tailor hardware to recurring workloads and improve productive capacity within constrained power envelopes. They also provide negotiating leverage when hyperscalers continue buying merchant processors. Arm supplies architecture and design building blocks while the hyperscaler retains control over deployment, software optimization and cloud-service pricing.

Alphabet’s use of Axion alongside TPUs is particularly important because it extends vertical optimization across host processing and acceleration. Amazon and Microsoft can similarly deploy proprietary CPUs where workload characteristics support favorable economics while retaining alternative processors for compatibility or specialized requirements.

The benefit should not be translated directly into cloud-margin expansion. Savings may be passed to customers, reinvested in infrastructure or offset by depreciation, memory inflation and the expense of maintaining proprietary hardware teams. Higher workload capacity per megawatt can improve returns without reducing absolute capital expenditure.

Near-term catalysts are deployment and instance-availability updates, rather than a new earnings event implied by Arm’s call. The longer-duration shift is a stronger cost position and greater hardware differentiation through calendar 2027 and beyond. These companies should not be counted as independent diversification from an AI infrastructure portfolio merely because their revenue models differ from semiconductor suppliers.

META AND ORACLE GAIN DEPLOYMENT OPTIONS, BUT THE BENEFIT IS CAPACITY PRODUCTIVITY RATHER THAN IMMEDIATE CAPEX REDUCTION (READ-THROUGH 8)

Affected companies: Meta Platforms (META: United States); Oracle (ORCL: United States).

Direction and magnitude: Positive for infrastructure flexibility and potential compute productivity. Moderate strategic importance for Meta’s CPU roadmap; initially modest consolidated financial significance for Oracle’s additional instance offering. Neither implication supports an immediate quantified earnings increase.

Arm described Meta as the principal customer and stated that demand from Meta and other customers had exceeded expectations. Meta’s own announcement confirms a multigeneration co-development relationship. The stronger supply coverage therefore improves the credibility of an infrastructure program intended to support Meta’s general-purpose and AI workloads, rather than simply adding another prospective chip supplier.

For Meta, the mechanism is better workload density and a more tailored CPU roadmap. Improved host processing and orchestration can help utilize expensive accelerator infrastructure more effectively. However, Arm retains commercial semiconductor economics, and more efficient CPUs can enable additional workloads rather than produce lower absolute capital spending. The call does not establish a reduction in Meta’s GPU requirements or a direct replacement of NVIDIA accelerators.

For Oracle, an additional merchant Arm CPU broadens the compute portfolio without requiring Oracle to build a complete proprietary CPU development organization. It can improve customer choice, strengthen procurement alternatives and support workload-specific price-performance offerings.

The timing is important. Although the call said OCI instances were planned for 2027, the October 28 announcement specified fall 2027. Arm’s initial commercial deliveries in January through March 2027 should not be treated as the date of Oracle’s general availability. Oracle’s offering was also announced before the earnings call, making the new information primarily stronger supply and customer-demand confidence.

Near-term catalysts are Arm’s shipment readiness and Meta deployment disclosures. Oracle’s more specific commercial catalyst is fall 2027 availability. Longer-term value depends on production workload performance and utilization, not the direct application of a modeled 2x rack-performance claim to either company’s total infrastructure costs.

SERVER SYSTEMS AND INTEGRATION

NAMED SYSTEM BUILDERS RECEIVE A REAL PRODUCT OPPORTUNITY, BUT REVENUE DOES NOT EQUAL CASH GENERATION (READ-THROUGH 9)

Affected companies: Super Micro Computer (SMCI: United States); Lenovo Group (0992: Hong Kong).

Direction and magnitude: Positive for the relevant server and integration businesses. Initially modest or unquantified at the consolidated level, with working-capital and component-cost risks limiting the certainty of profit conversion.

The relationship is explicit. Asked about the reference server design, management identified Supermicro, Lenovo and ASRock and stated, “They are building the racks for us.” This is a stronger basis for assigning exposure than general participation in an Arm ecosystem or an AI-related product announcement.

The transmission mechanism is demand for server design, assembly, integration, deployment and associated support around Arm AGI CPU. The processor creates another platform that system vendors can offer to cloud and enterprise customers. Standardized implementations may also broaden adoption beyond customers capable of creating their own complete hardware stack.

The upside should not be equated with Arm’s $2 billion cumulative chip-revenue opportunity. Arm did not disclose rack orders, allocation among partners or system selling prices. Nor did it establish that the opportunity would be material to each partner’s existing revenue base. Supermicro had already reported quarterly revenue of $19.9 billion on November 3, demonstrating why a new processor program should not automatically drive a large consolidated estimate increase.

The cash distinction is equally important. Supermicro’s same release reported a 12.8% adjusted gross margin but $434 million of operating cash outflow. That is not evidence that Arm systems will be unprofitable. It illustrates how rapid hardware growth can absorb cash through inventory, receivables and component procurement. Arm’s own discussion of memory, substrates and testing reinforces the need to evaluate complete-system availability and funding, not processor supply alone.

Near-term catalysts are partner order disclosures and qualification milestones ahead of January through March 2027 shipments. The longer-duration opportunity is a broader Arm server portfolio. The strongest high-conviction conclusion is positive product exposure, not guaranteed margin expansion or free-cash-flow accretion.

AUTOMOTIVE AND EMBEDDED COMPUTE

QUALCOMM’S AUTOMOTIVE DIVERSIFICATION HAS SUPPORT, WITHOUT IMPLYING A BROAD AUTO-SEMICONDUCTOR RECOVERY (READ-THROUGH 10)

Affected company: Qualcomm (QCOM: United States).

Direction and magnitude: Positive for automotive compute and the durability of diversification away from handsets. Material to the automotive business and increasingly relevant to consolidated revenue, but insufficient by itself to offset all handset weakness.

Arm reported 50% growth in physical AI royalties, specifically attributing the increase to advanced driver assistance and in-vehicle infotainment. Those applications provide a direct economic connection to Qualcomm’s automotive compute business. The signal is stronger for rising processing content per vehicle than for an increase in total vehicle production.

Qualcomm’s November 4 results independently reported automotive revenue of $1.990 billion, up 89%, representing approximately 19% of reported consolidated quarterly revenue. The Arm and Qualcomm growth rates cover different revenue bases and should not be equated. Together, however, they corroborate the mechanism: more sophisticated digital cockpits and driver-assistance functions can raise semiconductor content even when other electronics markets remain
