This is all wrong, though. 

Britain got into WWI for essentially three hard security reasons: The competition with Germany over naval dominance in the North Sea, the concomitant fear that German militarization of the Channel coast by seizing Belgium would allow a staging area for an invasion (always a “hard ‘no’”), and the reality that Britain (through its “military conversations” with France) was already engaged in Continental balance of power politics and in fact needed to be for the preceding two reasons. 

Those are all excellent reasons to get involved in a war, and yet the amazing thing is that there was such a debate in the British government about intervention at the time of the July Crisis that historians still dispute which, if any, of them truly forced Britain’s hand (leading, ironically, to this very dispute). 

Britain was the consummate reluctant warrior - and yet its back was to the wall.  

British statecraft in the early 20C is actually a model for how to manage an increasingly tight imperial security situation - if they couldn’t stay out, you have to wonder if anyone could. 

And, in fact, while there is always a pull back and forth in British strategy between the Continent and global empire/naval affairs, every hegemonic war since 1492 has seen British power either deployed to the Continent or (rarely, but it happens) Continental power deployed against Britain. 

Here are the data points: 
—The Italian Wars saw fighting over Calais (which England lost) as well as a French-supported (per the Auld Alliance) Scottish invasion of England (turned back at Flodden, Britain’s answer to Antietam) 
—The War of Dutch Independence included the War of the Armada; the follow-on 30 Years War manifested in Britain as the English Civil War (and yes - they’re related - affairs on the Continent feature in the 19 Propositions, and Puritan fear that Charles’ Arminianism and absolutism amounted to crypto-Catholicism is a standard feature in histories of it) 
—The Spanish Succession War and the preceding wars of Louis XIV saw an Anglo-Dutch alliance and, famously, Marlborough’s army deployed to the Continent 
—The Napoleonic Wars, of course, featured Wellington’s army in Spain and then at Waterloo 

The World Wars were just one more instance. And in fact this was well-understood by British leaders at the time and even by the British public. 

The “it was all for nothing” narrative is a (very) latecomer - it’s a recycling of German war angst (of the All Quiet On The Western Front variety, double-distilled by “nie wieder Krieg” after they got beaten the second time) via EU propaganda (have to marry your neighbor to avoid fighting them, you see). 

Britain still, to this day, doesn’t really buy it - the tone of Remembrance Day ceremonies tends to be solemn, but the dominant themes are gratitude and memory, not cynicism or disgust. As they should be.

Training Your Service Dog, Part 25: Ignore Offers of Food or Pets

Saturday, Nov 7, 2026

Part 24 taught heeling past food on the floor. This part covers the next public distraction: people who offer food or pets while the dog is working.

American Kennel Club public manners guidance (@AKCDogLovers) keeps the handler in charge of the greeting. Politely decline the offer. The dog holds heel or settle. Mark the ignore and pay from your pocket. Never take food from strangers. Never allow pets mid work. Food stays the daily training paycheck.

On a Tampa Bay outing, pick a Pinellas store path or cafe sidewalk. After a clean heel past floor food from Part 24, ask a helper to make ONE food or pet offer. Hold heel or settle. Mark ignore and continue. Keep the leash on. Never yell the dog's name. No loud NO. Approach calmly and keep dogs on our schedule.

Under US Department of Justice ADA guidance (@CivilRights), the dog stays harnessed or leashed unless that interferes, and removal is allowed only if out of control or not housebroken.

How to measure progress: aim for 8 of 10 clean ignores of one food or pet offer across 2 public places this week. Here in Tampa Bay, Odin is an 8 1/2 year old golden who started functional tasks at 6 months with Ski, and ignoring offers kept public work on schedule.

Watch Dogs of Service from Iowa PBS on YouTube

Sources: American Kennel Club public manners and leave it guidance, US Department of Justice ADA guidance, International Association of Assistance Dog Partners Minimum Training Standards for Public Access, photos of Odin by DigitalAssetsUS.

text:
#SunshineThroughTheRain Ep. 5–6:
Silly me...I didn't realise that on Netflix the episodes are available, unlike Mango TV and their frustrating SVIP setup. Hmmmm... anyway, I am SO SO INVESTED in this pairing, and especially in the quiet, heavy resilience of our little bittermelon, Zheng Yu. 

Chen Yan Zhou is right: this girl really can't catch a break. It feels as though life's misfortunes all conspired to land on her shoulders at once - a mother in a vegetative state, mounting medical bills, looming debts, eating expired rice balls and juggling multiple jobs. Then to see her get physically cornered and beaten, and instead of seeking help, choosing to weaponize that pain just to negotiate for compensation... it breaks your heart. Watching those loan sharks track her to the hospital, only for her to get chewed out by her boss for being late - until she finally snaps and yells back, immediately followed by the quiet ache of guilt because she realizes he carries the heavy burden of a special-needs son....gosh, it’s just too much. Mind you, she has a father who chose to abandon her and her mother, walking away with only his son. My tears for her are falling like a waterfall.

Yet, beneath all that raw survival mode, what I really want is for Zheng Yu to realize it's okay to finally lower her guard. It's so complex, isn't it? She isn't just rejecting love; she is terrified of pity and desperate not to feel even more indebted to a world that has only taken from her. But every little ray of sunshine- her dorm mates, the perfume girl, Aunty Yang, and now Chen Yan Zhou - is slowly chipping away at that armor. I have to commend Yang Chuo Yue here; she is so well cast as Zheng Yu, delivering such a layered, grounded performance where you can actually feel the ice inside melting away bit by bit.

And then there’s Chen Yan Zhou. After misjudging her early on, seeing her harsh reality firsthand and realizing how she quietly helped clear his name in the cheating scandal becomes a turning point for him. For a social misfit who doesn't quite know how to connect, he’s learning that the most profound thing he can offer her isn't grand gestures, but the steady presence of a true friend.

I am so excited by the ending of Episode 6 ...discovering that her new student is his cousin! Seeing how hopeful the previews for Episodes 7 and 8 look, it finally feels like things are genuinely looking up for our girl.

text:
#SunshineThroughTheRain Ep. 3–4
 I want to recommend this drama, especially if you like a comfort story that starts in the hardest of places yet still finds its way to hope and light. I know it’s a youth college romance, but its emotional core will resonate with almost any viewer. As I mentioned before, the main charm lies in the aloof, nearly wordless interactions between the leads. They are two extreme introverts, likely with thinking  (T) personalities, who waste no words, yet somehow understand each other and strike up a strange, quiet camaraderie, even with a few misunderstandings along the way.  

In Episode 3, things progress nicely as they team up for assignments and competitions, with him using her translation services to improve his thesis. There’s a wonderful moment (in this vid)  where she actually smiles for the very first time - right when she gives him live access to her working on his thesis and he types back some comments. This drama really thrives in these understated details. 

Although they misread each other initially, the story quickly shows them tuning into each other's situations. By Episode 4, you can genuinely see her ice melting as she starts taking an interest in his backstory. Unfortunately, a raw nerve gets struck when she asks an innocent question and discovers who his older brother was: a former top student who died a few years ago. There's definitely some trauma there on his end.  Deeply upset, he immediately retreats back into his shell, drawing a line between them. 

To make matters worse, he is falsely accused of cheating, a campus scandal that threatens to drag her down too, since they're partners for an upcoming academic competition. (Clearly, he's being framed, and I suspect the guy who has a crush on her is behind it.) Things are tense between them now, but I actually welcome this kind of conflict; it's a necessary step toward stripping away their remaining prejudices and assumptions about each other.

text:
#SunshineThroughTheRain Ep2

Crap, Zheng Yu ...her bitter life and that armor-plated inner monologue are really pulling me in. I feel for her, and it makes total sense why she comes across to everyone like a ghost, completely void of emotion. When you're a college kid juggling relentless part-time gigs just to cover medical bills while trying to claw your way toward an important internship, vulnerability is a luxury you can't afford. She's battle-hardened simply to survive, too proud, or rather, too terrified of being indebted, to accept even a shred of kindness from her dorm mates, pushing everyone away.

Fortunately, the frost is starting to crack a little, especially with Yan Zhou quietly observing her and potentially becoming that steady warmth.

First came his realization that the wallet incident wasn't her fault at all, breaking his initial suspicion. But the real shift happened when they both discovered neither of them secured the internship spot. Her inner monologue just hits right: "Even though we both lost, I feel less alone than if I had won... it's just a confirmation in this world that someone else is also standing in the rain like you."

That really got me. Consider me sold.

P/s I put together a few cuts of her narration here (sorry about the poor edit)

text:
Part of me wonders if Arch Manning will quit playing football after this season. 

I’m the only person in America saying this out loud. 

Why am I saying this?

I’ve studied every single snap Manning has played in college and there has been such a dramatic change in him from when I first began evaluating him on his 2023 and 2024 spot reps behind Quinn Ewers until now…

And it all continues to consistently trend in the wrong direction 📉

Back on his 2023 and 2024 reps he played with tempo and he looked confident. 

He looks like a different guy now.

Truth be told, Manning has not looked comfortable as the Longhorns’ starter from opening day in 2025.

He has not looked comfortable in his own skin. 

This season he hasn’t even looked comfortable in his uniform as he’s always doing this thing with his arm trying to loosen up.

Manning looked far more comfortable in the backup role behind Ewers. 

Here’s the other thing—

Manning does not look like he is having fun out there anymore. 

He’s legit smiled one time this season after winning against Ole Miss in his post game interview.

He’s looked like he’s had to try to work himself up to be confident and he’s looked passive aggressive. 

He does lot look like he is having fun out there anymore. 

Is it too much pressure for him being a starter? 

Is it too much pressure for him trying to live up to his last name?

Is it too much pressure for him trying to develop and to become “NFL-ready?” 

Those are questions only he can answer, but I can tell everybody this, there is something off about him. 

Something is not right. 

Here’s the concerning part—

He’s becoming more and more careless and reckless running the ball.

He’s absorbing more and more heavy contact in the pocket.

It’s like he wants to feel pain. It’s like he wants to take a beating. He’s playing like he wants to get injured so that can be “his out.”

He’s hardly sliding or running out of bounds anymore. 

Something is going on with him. 

It’s almost like he hates himself. 

That’s what it looks like.

I don’t know where he goes from here. Even with all the surrounding support he has playing for a college powerhouse team, he hasn’t turned the corner in terms of his development. 

If anything, he’s further regressed this season. 

He’s not developing into a two-read quarterback. 

He’s stuck being a one-read quarterback whose strengths seem to be handing the ball off and throwing elementary short passes. 

He’s also looks very moody during the games. He’s very “hot” and “cold” in terms of his performances in these games. He’s very streaky. His performance mirrors his body language in these games. 

Most of the time he looks down, lethargic, spaced out, sad, depressed, and like he’d rather be anywhere than behind center. 

I feel like he’s crying for help but nobody is listening.

I’m listening. 

I hear it.

I see it. 

It’s hard to miss.

It’s written all over him during these games and the cameras love to show him. 

That’s one of the advantages of studying televised game film vs. ALL-22. The televised game film captures the human element. 

What’s transferring to another school going to do besides make him some more NIL money?

What’s transferring to a lesser ranked program going to do for him besides offer him a softer schedule to throw against?

What’s that going to do besides get him overhyped and over-drafted in the NFL and really put him in a blender against an even higher level of competition? 

The most concerning part to me is Texas has tried to really dial it back to salvage him the past couple games. It’s been almost all one read throws like it was on his 2023 and 2024 reps, but it’s not working. It’s not restoring his confidence. 

I think all of this has been too much for him. 

What’s entering the 2027 NFL Draft going to do for him?

The skillset and mindset he’s put on tape so far this season does not project well to the NFL.

He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.
No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.
18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.
The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.
Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. 19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts.

20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.
Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.
He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First
21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.
For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.
Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.
22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.
China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.
Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.

Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.

After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.

Those are not tweets or campaign promises. They are changes in law, power, investment, sovereignty, culture, and the structure of the Republic itself. And they’re just the top 25: I could give you hundreds more.

8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan.
Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.
9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.
Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.
10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.
Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.
Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.
11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.
For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.
Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.
Trump Made Elections Matter Again
12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches.
In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.
Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.
Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.
13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse.
In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.
In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.
14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.
USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.
Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?
15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.
From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.
What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”
16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.
Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.
He Defended Faith and Family
17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform.
In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.
Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.
He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.
No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.
18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.
The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.
Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.
19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts.
As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.
That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.
20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.
Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.
He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First
21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.
For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.
Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.
22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.
China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.
Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.
23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months.
In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.
24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.
Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.
Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.
25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.
After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.
Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.
Now Act Like It Matters
Those are not tweets or campaign promises. They are changes in law, power, investment, sovereignty, culture, and the structure of the Republic itself. And they’re just the top 25: I could give you hundreds more.

text:
I have a new insecurity. 
It’s called wearable FOMO.

Apparently, a regular watch, two functioning wrists and ten perfectly good fingers are no longer enough!

The new corporate hi flier sports a smartwatch, a smart band, a smart ring and Meta glasses. 
Even silence must now be technologically enabled!
I decided “NOW OR NEVER! I SHALL ACQUIRE THE ACCESSORIES!” And that’s when trouble began.
Bands look good,I thought- 

Band A needs a subscription. 

Band B charges extra for deeper insights. 

Band C offers almost everything, except a few things you actually want!

Essentially, I was buying a device to tell me more about my health, provided I paid extra to find out!
Just as I was about to “Add to cart” the e-com platform hoodwinked me to check out the SMART RINGS. 

Apparently, a sensor around your finger is more accurate than one around your wrist.

At this rate, I expect a smart nose ring. Better proximity to the brain, perhaps?

I consulted my trusted LLM on how scientifically proven are the results-

HRV? Trends, not diagnosis.
Sleep stages? Educated guesses.
Stress? Indicative, not clinical.
Blood pressure? Don’t trust it.
Calories burnt? Approximate. Don’t use it to negotiate dessert!

A small fortune for a sophisticated collection of approximations!

I wondered what I’d actually do with all this data. So I asked my LLM!

Me: Can I use my sleep score to convince my boss I’ve been sleepless thinking about the project?

LLM: No.

Me: Can I use my HRV to convince my wife that my heartbeat rises whenever she’s around?

LLM: Don’t try too hard.

Fair point.

I then called my GP.

Me: Doctor, can I give your number to my wearable app so you can track my vitals?

GP: And why exactly do you see a need for it?

I had no answer. Perhaps he suspected Excessive Gadget Acquisition Syndrome!

NEW SNEAKERS, THEN! 
At least those could be a legitimate flex.

But then I spotted another entrant. The TEMPLE guys were taking pre-orders!

ENTROPY!

Back to traumatic memories of Thermodynamics in engineering college. 

As do the number of gadgets I need to reassure myself that I am healthy!

But seriously, what are we gaining by scattering our sleep, heartbeat, stress and movement data across multiple apps for them to monetise?

Aura farming? 
False security? 
Self-induced health anxiety in HD? 
A new corporate pecking order based on HRV and sleep scores?
Are we building healthier lives or simply better dashboards to worry about them?
We once wore expensive watches to show how successful we were.
Now we wear expensive devices to demonstrate how well we are sleeping.

I still haven’t bought anything.

But I’m sleep deprived researching about sleep trackers that I don’t even own!
Why don’t they just put a ring to the phone that I have a 10 hour screen time of? 
Never mind…

#Wearables #SmartTechnology #DigitalWellness #AI #Satire #FOMO 

(No wearable was harmed in this post)

text:
The Joyful Mysteries of the Rosary: Saturday November 07, 2026

A lamp still burning after midnight. A house too small for the news it holds. We pass locked screens and crowded rooms, and still the question waits. Where does real joy begin, if not in a yes spoken before the world is ready?

In the Joyful Mysteries we walk with Mary from the angel's greeting to the Child found in the Temple. At the Annunciation she receives the Word and offers her fiat. At the Visitation she carries Christ to Elizabeth, and charity becomes the first sermon. At the Nativity God enters our poverty in Bethlehem. At the Presentation the Holy Family obeys the Law, and Simeon recognizes the Light. In the Temple Jesus is found about his Father's work, and Mary keeps these things in her heart. We ask her to teach us that same hidden fidelity. Pray the Joyful Mysteries with us today.

I pray for you today 🙏 @RCatholicPrayer

text:
Thinking about this DPAS rating news right now, trying to figure out what it actually changes for the @AST_SpaceMobile thesis. And honestly, it completely flips my perspective on why they are building their own rocket.

Let me think out loud for a second.

On paper, getting a DPAS (Defense Priorities and Allocations System) rating from the U.S. government is incredible, as it means essentially that you have a federal VIP pass. If AST needs highly specialized parts, or more importantly, a launch slot on a SpaceX Falcon 9 or Blue Origin New Glenn, this rating legally forces the supplier to put our government-funded "BlackBird" satellites at the very front of the line. By law, you jump everyone else.

But here is where I start wondering: that VIP pass only applies to the 'BlackBirds' government contracts, right? It offers absolutely zero protection for our commercial BlueBirds. (Someone correct me if I’m wrong, but that's how DPAS works: it's tied to the contract, not the company

Now, combine that with the reality of the aerospace industry right now. There is a brutal shortage of heavy rockets. SpaceX is prioritizing Starlink. ULA and Ariane are booked out for years. New Glenn was delayed after the explosion. Launch slots are incredibly scarce. Upcoming Neutron rocket already booked in advance, with Peter Beck that they need to be 'extremely careful choosing their own customers', and 'the most important customer will be ourselves and our constellations'.

So, think about what happens when launch capacity is tight, and the DoD starts slapping DPAS priority ratings on the few available rockets out there. The unrated commercial payloads (like our standard telecom BlueBirds) could be just get bumped down the manifest,  over and over again.

If we strictly rely on third-party launch providers, we risk watching our commercial rollout stall completely just because someone else's priority payload took our seat. 
Now re-read and think about @AbelAvellan tweet: 'We are done waiting...' Is he referring exactly to that ?
We can't build a global cellular network by hoping there’s a spare spot on a competitor's rocket.

That’s why the BlackLift rocket suddenly makes total sense for the long term. It isn't a distraction or an ego project. When the rest of the industry is fighting for scraps of launch capacity, having our own dedicated pipeline to orbit is the only way to guarantee our commercial birds actually fly when we need them to.

It will launch in 2028 or 2030 or 2032? Honestly, IMO, who cares? We will book all launches that we need till that moment. Having in mind that we already booked in advance the deployment of 100 sats, ensuring us global coverage.

text:
🇳🇬🗳️ Tinubu’s Ibom Deep Seaport Approval Set to Transform South-South as Uyo and Calabar Prepare to Rival Lagos

President Bola Tinubu’s approval of the proposed Ibom Deep Seaport has raised hopes of a major economic transformation in Nigeria’s South-South, potentially positioning Uyo and nearby Calabar as formidable commercial counterparts to Lagos.

Announcing the decision on Friday at a rally in Uyo, the Akwa Ibom capital, Tinubu endorsed Governor Umo Eno’s request for the long-awaited maritime project and promised development that would reach beyond the state.

The proposed port could reshape trade across the region, attracting manufacturers, logistics operators, exporters and investors while creating opportunities for thousands of workers. Alongside Calabar’s existing port infrastructure, it offers the prospect of a stronger maritime corridor capable of sharing business activity now concentrated around Lagos and the South-West.

For Akwa Ibom, the opportunity extends far beyond shipping. Industrial parks, warehousing, road transport, hospitality and agricultural processing could all benefit if the project secures financing, efficient connections and timely construction.

Tinubu also approved the upgrade of Victor Attah International Airport to international status, strengthening Uyo’s ambitions to become an aviation and commercial hub. The President said infrastructure investments must create lasting economic value and support inclusive growth.

The announcement provides a significant boost to Eno, who has made the seaport a central demand of his administration. It also complements plans for greater coastal connectivity, including the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway.

Tinubu used the occasion to draw a sharp political contrast with opposition presidential hopeful Peter Obi. Referring to Obi’s record as Anambra governor, he accused him of failing to confront the state’s erosion crisis.

“I, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, confronted the Atlantic Ocean,” the President declared, invoking coastal protection and land reclamation efforts associated with his time governing Lagos. His criticism of Obi remains a political allegation rather than an independent assessment of their records.

The Ibom project is still at the planning and procurement stage, and its economic promise will depend on implementation. Nevertheless, Friday’s endorsement offers the South-South an opportunity to build a competitive new growth centre.

If delivered, the port could help Uyo and Calabar challenge Lagos’s longstanding dominance, giving Nigeria a more balanced, diversified and prosperous coastal economy in coming decades.

text:
US Launches Task Force Iron Gate To Cut Iran's Land Routes

US Central Command has expanded its pressure campaign against Iran beyond the sea, with the creation of a dedicated task force to disrupt Tehran's overland and Caspian supply networks.

On 7 Nov CENTCOM Commander Adm.Brad Cooper directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, a compact interagency staff of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida.

Its mandate is to coordinate across US government agencies to monitor, detect, and disrupt the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illicit revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

'The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea,' said Cooper. 'Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with US interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military.'

The move represents a significant evolution in US strategy -  a shift from maritime containment to a comprehensive, multi-domain interdiction effort.

At sea, the blockade has already had a profound effect. First imposed on 13 Apr following the collapse of negotiations, briefly lifted after the Jun ceasefire, and reimposed on 14-15 Jul after renewed attacks on commercial shipping, it has, according to CENTCOM, prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil in recent months. Enforcement remains in force against all vessels entering or departing Iranian ports.

On land, the challenge is more complex - CENTCOM's own operational focus includes Iran's borders with Türkiye, Afghanistan, Turkmenistan, and Pakistan, a vast and porous geography that cannot be policed by naval power alone.

The inclusion of the Caspian Sea is particularly consequential. A June 2026 assessment by the Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), titled Preventing Iran's Military Reconstitution, identified the Caspian as a likely substitute route for military-related procurement as traditional maritime channels close.

The logic is geographic - the Caspian gives Iran direct access to Russia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Turkmenistan, with its northern ports of Bandar Anzali and Amirabad positioned as natural entry points for industrial equipment, military components, and dual-use technologies.

It is also legally distinct - u/the 2018 Convention on the Legal Status of the Caspian Sea, armed forces from outside the five littoral states are barred from operating there, and vessels must fly the flag of one of those states. The United States, therefore, has no direct naval presence in the Caspian, a constraint that makes interagency coordination, intelligence-sharing, and partner engagement essential rather than optional.

Reporting already suggests this corridor is active. Russian vessels are said to have delivered drone components, ammunition, and explosives to Amirabad, alongside civilian cargo such as wheat, corn, and animal feed, a blending of military and commercial shipments that complicates enforcement.

Pakistan presents a parallel concern. The CSIS assessment identified the shared Iran-Pakistan border as a potential overland corridor for commercial and dual-use goods. With barter mechanisms, TIR Carnets, and eased transit arrangements facilitating trade toward Central Asia, cargo movement through Balochistan and onward rail links through Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan offers Tehran additional avenues to circumvent traditional banking scrutiny.

The u/lying imperative is reconstitution. Following US and Is*aeli strikes in 2026, Iran is assessed to have expended roughly 60% of its drone inventory, retaining approx.40%. To rebuild, it will require drone components, precision machine tools, marine engines and gearboxes, and salvage equipment to clear sunken vessels obstructing ports such as Bandar Abbas and Bushehr.

Historically, much of this material arrived as reexports through the UAE. With that route no longer viable, CSIS assesses that rerouting through Pakistan and the Caspian Sea, alongside more direct sourcing from China, represents the most probable alternative.

The report further cautions that Iran brings over 4-decades of experience in operating covert acquisition networks worldwide. Its recommendations reflect that reality  - extend EU-style no-reexport provisions to Iran, engage third countries before new transshipment networks consolidate, and assist US and allied firms in identifying high-risk transactions in China and Türkiye.

Tehran's response was swift, on the same day, IRGC spokesperson Brig Gen Hossein Mohebbi claimed Iran was not only meeting domestic requirements but was also exporting systems such as the Arman missile, the 358 loitering munition, and the Khordad-3 air defence system

Taken together, Task Force Iron Gate signals Washington's recognition that a sea blockade alone is insufficient, the contest over Iran's rearmament will now be decided as much on land and on the Caspian as at sea.

text:
AM I OPPRESSED?

I grew up in a place where a woman could decide for herself how she wanted to dress.

Where nobody dictated how much of her body she was allowed to show. Where clothing, modesty, and personal appearance were matters of individual choice, not government mandates.

I grew up believing that freedom meant having a choice.

I could dress modestly. I could dress boldly. I could cover myself from head to toe or choose not to. Nobody needed to approve. Nobody needed to give me permission.

But now I find myself in a society where the law tells me I must cover up.

Where my clothing is no longer entirely my decision. Where the government determines what is acceptable for a woman to wear in public, and stepping outside those boundaries can have legal consequences.

I don’t mind covering up. That’s not the point.

The point is choice.

I find it fascinating how quickly people recognize oppression when they believe it is happening in another culture, yet how easily they overlook restrictions when they happen in their own backyard.

So, am I oppressed?

You probably think I’m describing life in Saudi Arabia, Iran, or another conservative country where women’s clothing is regulated by law.

But no.

I’m talking about the United States of America. More specifically, Georgia.

And here’s where the irony becomes even more interesting.

I grew up in Germany. In Munich, I can enjoy designated nude beaches and bathing areas, visit public swimming facilities where topless sunbathing is permitted, and enjoy designated clothing-optional spaces right in the middle of the city. In some designated areas, nudity is perfectly legal.

And it’s not just Germany. In Italy, France, Spain, Norway and Denmark, women enjoy freedoms in public bathing and designated naturist spaces that are restricted in many parts of the United States.

In many of these European countries, a woman’s decision to go topless or enjoy a nude beach is not automatically treated as a criminal matter.

Yet here I am, in the so-called land of the free, where in Georgia and other conservative American states, even going topless in public can have legal consequences.

Think about that for a moment.

Europe is supposedly the place Americans sometimes criticize for being too liberal, too permissive, or lacking traditional values.

Yet when it comes to allowing women to make decisions about their own bodies, many European countries offer considerably more freedom than the United States.

I don’t need to be topless. I don’t need to be naked. I don’t need to prove my freedom by what I wear or don’t wear.

But I do believe that the choice should be mine.

Because freedom isn’t the right to tell women how to dress according to YOUR values.

Freedom is allowing women to make that decision for themselves.

And perhaps before lecturing the rest of the world about the oppression of women, America should take a good look in the mirror.

Lecture: 
Reconstructive Memory, 
Institutional Emergence, 
and the Displacement of Expertise 
in Correctional Mental Health

(For graduate students in 
Law, 
Political Science, 
Psychiatry, and 
Social Anthropology)

On this day three years ago, 
a photograph circulated: 
a snow-laden tree in a parking lot, 
a blue institutional sign, 
and, as one commenter noted, 
the police still visible in the background. 

The post was made from Anchorage.

Today the same person 
sits in the high desert 
of Piñon, Arizona, 
at roughly 6,000 feet, 
where the air is dry and the light is hard. 

Memory does not simply retrieve; 
it reconstructs 
under the pressure of the present environment,
 the temperature of the day, 
and the residual institutional aftertaste. 

This is the material 
we will examine 
through five interlocking lenses.

1. Self-Organizing Systems
Correctional mental-health units 
are not designed 
from a blueprint of optimal care; 

they emerge 
rom interacting constraints: 
statutory mandates for treatment, 
fixed budgets, 
staffing shortages, 
and the legal status of providers. 

In Alaska, 
psychiatric mental-health nurse practitioners 
hold full practice authority. 

They evaluate, diagnose, and prescribe 
without physician supervision 
or a collaborative agreement. 

In a system 
already organized around cost containment, 
this legal fact 
becomes an attractor.

 Minimalist management 
does not need to issue a formal directive 
to “replace psychiatrists”; 
the cheaper, 
independently licensed provider 
simply becomes the equilibrium state. 

The psychiatrist 
who held the contract 
from August to late December 2023 
at Anchorage Correctional Complex West 
and Hiland Mountain 
is displaced 
not by malice 
but by the self-organization 
of a complex adaptive system 
under fiscal pressure. 

From an anthropological standpoint, 
the traveling 1099 contractor 
is himself 
an adaptive agent 
moving across climates 
and regulatory regimes; 

from a psychiatric standpoint, 
the clinical culture
 of the unit reconfigures 
around whoever can sign the orders 
at lower unit cost.

2. Plausible Deniability
No memorandum 
need declare 
that board-certified psychiatrists are expendable. 

The decision 
can be framed as 
“workforce flexibility,” 
“access expansion,” or
 “fiscal responsibility.” 

Because Alaska law 
authorizes independent psychiatric practice 
by nurse practitioners, 
management 
can truthfully say 
it has complied with all licensing requirements. 

Liability is diffused: 
the facility met the letter of the law; 
the individual provider 
met the regulatory standard for his or her license. 

In memory, the same structure operates. 

The snowy tree photograph is real, 
the police car was present, 
yet the precise affective charge 
of that day is reconstructed 
under Arizona light. 

The mind offers itself plausible deniability 
about what it felt then 
versus what it feels now. 

Law students 
will recognize the parallel 
in standard-of-care arguments; 

political scientists 
will see it in the language
 of public-sector reform; 

anthropologists 
will note how institutions 
narrate continuity 
while rearranging personnel.

3. Murphy’s Law
If a contract can end at the close of December,
 it will. 

If the replacement 
can be accomplished with a lower-cost provider a
lready authorized to practice psychiatry 
independently, 
that substitution will occur. 

If the departing clinician 
must then relocate to a warmer climate 
(Skyview Unit, Rusk, Texas, January–March 2024),
 the logistics will introduce their own frictions. 

Murphy’s Law is not mysticism; 
it is the observation 
that in tightly coupled systems
—correctional schedules, 
credentialing timelines, 
weather, 
and human preference for lower unit cost
—failure modes 
that are possible become probable. 

The psychiatrist’s normal 
of serial 1099 contracts 
is itself an adaptation to this regularity. 

Psychiatry students s
hould note 
that clinical continuity 
is among the first casualties; 

law students 
should note 
that the resulting gaps 
are rarely actionable 
if each provider 
was properly licensed 
at the time of service.

4. Pandora’s Box
Full practice authority 
was opened 
with the intention of increasing access 
and reducing cost. 

Once opened, 
it also released 
the possibility of systematic substitution. 

Expertise differentials
—years of residency,
 forensic experience, 
the capacity to manage 
high-acuity correctional caseloads
—are not automatically preserved by statute. 
The box does not close. 

Political scientists 
observe the classic policy feedback: 
a regulatory change 
alters incentives, 
which alter staffing patterns, 
which alter the political constituency 
for the original rule. 

Anthropologists 
observe the cultural shift 
inside the units: 
the social meaning of “psychiatrist” 
changes 
when the role 
can be filled by a different professional category. 

The individual 
who flew from Anchorage to Texas 
at the end of December 
experienced one personal consequence 
of that opening.

5. The Butterfly Effect
A seemingly technical provision i
n Alaska’s nurse-practice act
—independent authority 
for psychiatric nurse practitioners
—interacts with
budget offices, 
contracting firms, 
and individual career paths. 

One small regulatory flap 
produces a cascade: 
contract non-renewal, 
geographic relocation, 
a Facebook memory 
that surfaces 
three years later 
under a different sky, 
and a lecture
 constructed in Piñon about Anchorage. 

The effect is not deterministic; 
other states maintain collaborative 
or supervisory requirements 
and produce different staffing equilibria. 

Yet once the Alaska equilibrium is established, 
the downstream trajectories 
of particular clinicians 
become sensitive to that initial condition. 

Law 
tracks the statutory origin; 

political science 
tracks the interest-group 
and budgetary amplifiers; 

psychiatry 
tracks the clinical texture of care 
under the new staffing regime; 

anthropology 
tracks the lived experience 
of the mobile professional 
whose memory 
is continually rewritten 
by successive climates.

Across the four disciplines 
the same phenomena appear 
under different names: 
regulatory federalism 
and scope-of-practice doctrine 

(Law); 
policy feedback
 and bureaucratic rationalization 

(Political Science); 
training gradients, 
continuity of care, 
and institutional psychiatry 

(Psychiatry); 
situated knowledge, 
environmental reconstruction of memory, 

(Social Anthropology).
and the ethnography 
of professional mobility 

The snowy tree with the police still visible 
is not merely a personal souvenir. 

It is a small, 
durable trace 
of a larger self-organizing process 
whose plausible deniability,
 predictable frictions, 
opened possibilities, 
and sensitive dependencies 
continue to shape 
who practices, 
under what authority, 
and at what remembered temperature.

Do It Again
(after Steely Dan)

You signed the papers in the cold
Nurse practitioners holding the fold
Independent license, cheaper by half
Minimalist CEO doing the math

You packed the bags when December broke
Flew to Texas where the weather spoke
Skyview Unit, warmer light

But the contract ends on a Friday night
You go back, Jack, do it again
Wheels turn, weather changes, same old spin

Memory reconstructs under the sun
Piñon desert, Anchorage done
The tree was heavy with November snow

Blue sign standing, police in the glow
Someone said the picture was fine
But you still see the car in the line

High desert now at six thousand feet
Dry air rewriting the cold you meet
Three years later the post appears

Environment edits the earlier years
You go back, Jack, do it again
Full practice authority sets the scene

Plausible reasons, Murphy arrives
Pandora’s open, the butterfly flies
Self-organizing, no one to blame

System finds the lower-cost name
You keep moving, 1099
Another unit, another skyline

Snow to heat, heat to recall
The police stay visible after allY
ou go back, Jack, do it again

Turn the page, sign the form, and begin
Memory’s weather, institutional rain
You go back, Jack, do it again.

text:
$SUN KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM SUNOCO AND SUNOCOCORP Q3 2026 EARNINGS CALL

Sunoco’s results reinforce a differentiated downstream investment thesis: constrained product supply and volatile wholesale prices are supporting refining and fuel-distribution profitability even as underlying consumption softens. The strongest actionable read-through is favorable operating conditions for fuel distributors reporting after Sunoco, rather than a broad acceleration in petroleum demand. Direct ownership economics also transmit Sunoco’s stronger distributions to Energy Transfer. Over a longer horizon, the same regional product shortages supporting exceptional refinery margins are encouraging infrastructure investment that could redistribute those profits toward transportation and integrated supply networks. The distinction between earnings and cash realization remains important: Sunoco’s record EBITDA coexisted with a DCF miss, while regional demand, acquisition effects and financing requirements prevent uniform extrapolation across downstream equities. The conclusions below distinguish incremental information from corroboration of results already reported.

FUEL DISTRIBUTION AND CONVENIENCE RETAIL

MARGIN RESILIENCE IS A MORE ACTIONABLE SIGNAL THAN GALLON GROWTH (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected companies: Global Partners LP (GLP: United States), CrossAmerica Partners LP (CAPL: United States) and Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. (ATD: Canada).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for fuel gross profit, with moderate potential earnings significance. Global Partners and CrossAmerica offer the clearest near-term reporting catalysts. The evidence supports favorable margin conditions, but does not establish a consensus earnings beat for any individual company.

Call evidence: Sunoco generated $532 million of Fuel Distribution EBITDA excluding transaction expenses, versus $516 million in Q2, despite fuel margin declining slightly to 16.8 cents per gallon. Management described U.S. diesel demand as approximately flat and gasoline demand as down low single digits. Austin Harkness emphasized that wholesale prices had not yet “durably come off, which is where we tend to see the most margin expansion.”

The transmission mechanism is retained distribution and retail margin, not higher commodity revenue. Volatility creates procurement and inventory-management opportunities, while a sustained decline in wholesale acquisition costs can temporarily widen retail margins when pump prices adjust more slowly. Terminal access, supply alternatives and transportation flexibility improve the ability to capture these opportunities. Consequently, modestly declining gallons need not imply declining fuel earnings.

Global Partners provides particularly relevant corroboration. Its Q2 gasoline-distribution product margin increased to $175.0 million from $137.9 million even though Gasoline Distribution and Station Operations volumes declined to 351.2 million gallons from 382.4 million. That demonstrates actual margin compensation for lower volumes within the peer’s own business. At the Q2 volume base, each additional 1 cent per gallon of retained margin would represent approximately $3.5 million of quarterly gross profit before incremental expenses and other adjustments. This is a sensitivity, not a forecast of the realized margin change.

CrossAmerica’s Q2 results similarly showed a 33% increase in retail fuel margin per gallon and a 20% increase in retail fuel gross profit despite a 12% decline in retail gallons. However, its wholesale volume decline also reflected lost independent-dealer contracts. Sunoco’s favorable industry commentary does not eliminate that company-specific customer-retention problem. The read-through is positive to the pricing environment, not evidence that CrossAmerica has reversed its volume deterioration.

Couche-Tard’s latest reported quarter showed U.S. fuel gross margin increasing to 52.61 cents per gallon from 44.00 cents, while U.S. same-store fuel volumes declined 1.6%. That independently validates the margin-versus-volume mechanism in a large retail network. Its Canadian exposure requires more caution because Sunoco described both gasoline and diesel demand there as down low to mid-single digits. Nevertheless, Couche-Tard had reported Canadian same-store fuel volume growth of 1.1% in its quarter ended July 19, illustrating that market demand and individual-chain performance can diverge.

Timing and investment implication: CrossAmerica’s November 4 results and Global Partners’ November 6 results are genuine near-term catalysts. The principal variables are realized fuel margin, customer retention and operating expenses, rather than reported revenue growth. For Couche-Tard, Sunoco’s commentary supports the next fiscal-quarter fuel-profit outlook but does not resolve merchandise performance or regional market-share changes. Falling wholesale prices represent additional conditional upside, not a necessary assumption for the favorable current-margin assessment.

CARIBBEAN GROWTH HAS A DIRECT PUBLIC-MARKET ANALOGUE IN RUBIS (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected company: Rubis SCA (RUI: France).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive, with meaningful regional exposure and moderate consolidated significance. This is primarily confirmation of an operating trend rather than an unreported Q3 earnings surprise.

Call evidence: Harkness described the Caribbean as “a growth engine for us” and expected continued growth from “both on healthy volume growth and margin expansion.” Management contrasted that performance with weaker Canadian demand and subdued U.S. consumption.

Rubis is a relevant comparison because it owns Caribbean fuel-distribution, retail, commercial-supply and aviation-fueling operations. The transmission mechanism is higher physical sales and retained commercial margins across its regional network. The exposure does not depend on Rubis supplying Sunoco or receiving a contract from it; the companies participate in overlapping regional fuel markets.

Rubis’s November 3 trading update independently supports the signal. Caribbean Q3 volumes increased approximately 6% to 651,000 cubic meters, while regional gross margin increased approximately 10% to €91 million. The Caribbean represented approximately 40% of the company’s Q3 Retail & Marketing gross margin. In H1, Caribbean Retail & Marketing EBITDA was €124 million against €434 million of consolidated EBITDA, establishing that the region is economically significant rather than incidental.

The detailed country mix is important. Rubis identified strong commercial activity in Haiti and Suriname and solid aviation traffic in Saint Lucia and Barbados. These disclosures support a regional growth thesis, but not a uniform assumption across every Caribbean market. Sunoco itself emphasized that its more than 20 markets have different demand and margin characteristics.

There are important limitations to the positive read-through. Rubis’s H1 Caribbean volumes increased faster than gross margin, and some reported EBITDA growth benefited from hyperinflation accounting. In addition, its SARA refinery operates under a distinct business model with relatively stable earnings. Sunoco’s exceptional Burnaby margin should not be transferred to SARA as an incremental refining-profit forecast.

Cash realization also tempers the earnings signal. Rubis’s H1 EBITDA increased 18%, but adjusted operating cash flow declined 19%, reflecting higher working-capital requirements associated with elevated oil prices. That adjusted measure already excluded the €64 million competition-related fine payment. Favorable distribution margins can therefore coexist with a substantial cash-funding requirement. Sunoco’s DCF weakness had different disclosed drivers, principally taxes and maintenance, but both cases caution against equating EBITDA growth with immediately distributable cash.

Timing and investment implication: Rubis had already released its Q3 update before Sunoco’s call and reaffirmed its €775 million to €825 million EBITDA guidance. Sunoco adds independent confirmation rather than a new earnings catalyst. The longer-duration positive is diversified Caribbean demand and commercial optimization; the negative offset is cash tied up in working capital while product prices remain elevated. Full-year results scheduled for March 11, 2027 should provide the more meaningful cash-conversion test.

MIDSTREAM OWNERSHIP AND REFINED-PRODUCT INFRASTRUCTURE

ENERGY TRANSFER RECEIVES A DIRECT CASH BENEFIT, BUT NOT SUNOCO’S ENTIRE EBITDA INCREASE (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected company: Energy Transfer LP (ET: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive and directly measurable, but modest relative to Energy Transfer’s consolidated cash generation. The effect is already reflected in its same-day results rather than an incremental earnings surprise.

Call evidence: Sunoco announced a quarterly distribution of $1.0148, approximately 10.3% above the year-earlier level, and reported trailing distribution coverage of 2.1x. Management also highlighted approximately 25% growth in DCF per common unit following Parkland and leverage of approximately 3.5x.

Energy Transfer owns Sunoco’s general-partner interests, incentive distribution rights and approximately 28 million common units. The direct economic transmission is therefore a combination of common-unit distributions and general-partner distributions. It is not simply a percentage participation in Sunoco’s consolidated EBITDA.

Energy Transfer’s November 3 DCF reconciliation reports $105 million of distributions from Sunoco in Q3, compared with $68 million a year earlier. The $37 million increase equals approximately 1.5% of Energy Transfer’s Q3 attributable DCF of $2.522 billion. Total Sunoco distributions represented approximately 4.2% of that DCF. The contribution is therefore meaningful within the downstream investment, but insufficient by itself to explain Energy Transfer’s broader earnings growth.

The accounting distinction is particularly important because Energy Transfer consolidates Sunoco. Its DCF reconciliation removes Sunoco’s consolidated DCF and adds back the distributions attributable to Energy Transfer. Treating Sunoco’s $1.049 billion of formal adjusted EBITDA, or its entire $588 million of adjusted DCF, as cash accruing to Energy Transfer investors would materially overstate the exposure.

The longer-duration benefit is the ability of Sunoco’s acquisition program and distribution growth to expand Energy Transfer’s cash receipts through its ownership and incentive rights. The corresponding risk is that acquisition financing, refinery normalization or weaker cash conversion reduces Sunoco’s future distribution-growth capacity. Strong current coverage makes immediate distribution stress unlikely, but the realized 10% year-over-year increase should not be assumed to recur indefinitely because Sunoco’s 2026 distribution included a special step-up.

Timing and investment implication: Energy Transfer had already reported the $105 million contribution before Sunoco’s call. The call reinforces the sustainability assessment but does not justify adding the benefit again to forecasts. The next actionable milestones are Sunoco’s 2027 guidance and subsequent distribution decisions, with the investment significance measured in attributable cash receipts rather than consolidated subsidiary EBITDA.

WESTBOUND PRODUCT FLOWS FAVOR CONTRACTED INFRASTRUCTURE OVER PURE SCARCITY EXPOSURE (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected companies: Kinder Morgan Inc. (KMI: United States), Phillips 66 (PSX: United States) and HF Sinclair Corporation (DINO: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for long-duration infrastructure earnings and supply flexibility. The project is significant within refined-product logistics but does not create a material 2026 earnings contribution. Construction spending is a near-term cash outflow.

Call evidence: Asked whether new westbound product routes could tighten Mid-Continent balances and increase demand for northbound Gulf Coast shipments, management responded that “the short answer is yes.” It also emphasized that the outcome depends on projects being built and product flows changing.

The relevant Western Gateway system has disclosed ownership of 49.9% for Phillips 66, 35.1% for Kinder Morgan and 15% for HF Sinclair. The sponsors announced final investment approval in August, with approximately 230,000 barrels per day of design capacity and a targeted 2029 completion, subject to permitting and regulatory approvals. Sunoco’s call therefore corroborates the commercial logic of an existing project; it does not announce a new award or investment decision.

The economic mechanism is a reconfiguration of regional supply. Greater access from Mid-Continent and Gulf Coast origins to Arizona and California can monetize transportation demand, improve refinery market access and reduce dependence on more expensive marginal supply routes. Primarily 10-year take-or-pay contracts support the pipeline’s revenue visibility, although contractual credit quality, operating costs and construction execution still determine returns.

Kinder Morgan’s capital structure within the project is particularly important. It plans to contribute existing SFPP assets valued at approximately $1.5 billion and approximately $250 million of cash. Its 35.1% interest is therefore not a nearly costless claim on a new pipeline. Existing asset earnings are being contributed, so incremental value must be measured against the earnings relinquished and the additional cash investment. Applying its ownership percentage to all future project EBITDA without this adjustment would overstate accretion.

Phillips 66 expects approximately $2.5 billion of cash contributions and also gains strategic connectivity between its refining and marketing positions. HF Sinclair expects approximately $750 million of contributions and gains a direct infrastructure interest alongside potential supply-chain benefits. Those commitments create execution and funding exposure before earnings begin.

The call supports possible secondary benefits for upstream feeder routes, but does not establish incremental tariffs or committed volumes for every interconnected pipeline. Additional throughput only creates incremental earnings where the owner has available capacity and retains an economic fee beyond existing contractual commitments.

Timing and investment implication: Permitting, construction progress, capital-cost control and eventual commissioning are the relevant catalysts. The fundamental shift is toward a more connected western fuel market, with a larger share of value captured through transportation contracts and integrated supply arrangements. The benefit should not be booked as a near-term earnings surprise or confused with the separate, already completed Denver expansion.

REFINING AND REGIONAL PRODUCT BALANCES

WESTERN REFINERS RETAIN STRONG NEAR-TERM CASH EARNING POWER (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected companies: HF Sinclair Corporation (DINO: United States) and PBF Energy Inc. (PBF: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive, with potentially high operating-earnings sensitivity. Incremental information value is lower than the operating magnitude because both companies had already reported Q3 before Sunoco’s call.

Call evidence: Burnaby generated $238 million of EBITDA, up from $175 million in Q2, with throughput of approximately 57,000 barrels per day and refining margin above $54 per barrel. Management attributed the favorable environment partly to “tight distillate inventories, global supply disruptions, refinery outages and fall maintenance activity.”

HF Sinclair’s Puget Sound refinery is a geographically relevant comparison because it operates in Washington and participates in Pacific Northwest product markets close to British Columbia. PBF’s Martinez and Torrance refineries provide exposure to California’s constrained product market. These are regional market exposures, not disclosed supplier or customer relationships with Sunoco.

The transmission mechanism is stronger realized product pricing relative to crude and operating costs, provided the refineries remain available and can produce the required product mix. Reliability is therefore essential. A favorable regional crack spread creates little value at an idled unit, and differences in feedstocks, product specifications, logistics and renewable-fuel compliance prevent direct transplantation of Burnaby’s $54 margin.

Peer disclosures substantiate the favorable environment. HF Sinclair reported Q3 adjusted refinery gross margin of $54.22 per produced barrel sold and refining adjusted EBITDA of $2.582 billion. However, its results also benefited from small-refinery RIN waivers, while an El Dorado turnaround reduced Mid-Continent sales. Those company-specific effects should not be attributed to the same mechanism as Burnaby’s results.

PBF reported approximately $2.112 billion of operating income excluding special items. Its Martinez refinery had returned to full operations in May, and the Martinez hydrocracker and Paulsboro turnarounds that commenced in September were completed in October. These operating milestones provide a stronger basis for evaluating Q4 earnings capture than regional margin strength alone.

PBF’s Q4 West Coast throughput guidance of 290,000 to 310,000 barrels per day provides an indication of sensitivity. At that activity level, a $1 per barrel change in retained margin represents approximately $27 million to $29 million of quarterly gross earnings exposure before taxes and other offsets. The calculation demonstrates materiality; it is not a prediction that PBF realizes Burnaby’s margin or that the regional spread will move by a particular amount.

Timing and investment implication: The near-term catalysts are Q4 realized margins, winter product balances and operating availability. Sunoco’s call supports continued favorable conditions but does not create another Q3 earnings beat for companies that already reported. Strong cash generation can improve balance sheets and support shareholder returns even if the earnings level proves temporary. The appropriate positive inference is cash-generation capacity, not permanent annualization of unusually favorable quarterly EPS.

NEW WESTERN SUPPLY ROUTES CHALLENGE THE DURATION OF CALIFORNIA REFINING SCARCITY PROFITS (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected company: PBF Energy Inc. (PBF: United States). Relevant relative beneficiaries: Phillips 66 (PSX: United States) and HF Sinclair Corporation (DINO: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Negative for the long-duration scarcity component of California refining margins, with potentially material valuation significance for PBF. This is not a near-term earnings-short thesis. Confidence is high in the competitive mechanism if the infrastructure enters service; the eventual margin effect remains uncertain.

Call evidence: The discussion of new routes linking Mid-Continent and Gulf Coast supply to western markets acknowledged that projects could alter regional balances. Separately, Kim repeatedly emphasized Sunoco’s ability to grow even if refining margins return toward mid-cycle. Together, those comments distinguish today’s favorable economics from a claim that current regional margins are permanent.

The transmission mechanism is lower-cost alternative supply. Greater access to inland and Gulf Coast products can reduce the price premium required to attract marginal barrels into Arizona and California. That can weaken the bargaining position of incumbent western refiners and reduce some of the regional scarcity value embedded in their earnings.

PBF is directly exposed through Martinez and Torrance, but is not among the disclosed Western Gateway owners. It therefore lacks the project-level transportation earnings that would partially offset a reduction in refining scarcity profits for the sponsors. Phillips 66 and HF Sinclair have more balanced exposure: potential pressure on some refining margins can coexist with pipeline income and improved access for other assets.

The prospective 230,000-barrel-per-day system is meaningful regional infrastructure, but that number must not be treated as 230,000 barrels per day of incremental California gasoline supply. Destinations include Arizona; product compatibility, connecting-system capacity, contractual allocations and displacement of existing shipments all matter. California fuel specifications and permitting requirements also constrain the extent of immediate substitution.

The negative implication is consequently about earnings duration and valuation rather than a quantified near-term EBITDA reduction. PBF’s current cash generation can still create substantial equity value through debt reduction and capital returns. However, capitalizing current California margins as a permanent scarcity annuity would ignore the investment response those same margins are encouraging.

Timing and investment implication: Western Gateway targets 2029 completion, with regulatory and construction uncertainty. The nearer-term catalysts are permits, execution milestones and firmer information on product destinations and commitments. Those developments can affect valuation before physical flows begin. The longer-duration relative preference is for businesses that monetize improved connectivity through contracts or integrated supply chains, rather than relying exclusively on persistent regional product shortages.

text:
Biden time, yet never living. A soulless corpse to mimic life. The trumpet blast ruptures the eardrum. Battle banging bound to strife. The figure at the center is not a person but a performance of presence, a body animated by other hands. Wuhan soup in flames of Waco. The two names are forced into the same spoon and the same fire. One is the origin story of a global stillness that emptied streets and accounts; the other is the older American memory of a compound set alight under federal authority. Tasting children, all enticed. Epstein Island sanitizing. Nothing to see, we’re all alright. The refrain returns, now as official statement. The island is cleaned; the records are managed; the children are either not children or not worth the disruption of order. Censorship is not merely the removal of speech; it is the maintenance of a surface on which the ordinary citizen can still say “we’re all alright.” The psychological cost is the slow training of the eye to slide past the stain. The metacognitive demand is immediate: notice what your own attention refuses to hold.

Mute the mouths that speak of evil. Scapegoat the civil and claim the lie. No whistle blows to hands that strangle. The grammar of accusation is reversed. Those who name the hands are the ones whose mouths must be stopped. Join us all in ties that bind. Submit yourself and become humble. Do not fight, for that’s unkind. Share your wealth, then share it double. Nothing to lose with nothing to hide. The moral inversion is complete and offered as virtue. Humility is no longer the recognition of limits; it is the surrender of the capacity to say no. Kindness is the refusal to resist. The Christ who forgives is pressed into service as the final argument against opposition. The line is sarcastic only in the sense that the sarcasm has already been institutionalized; the secular mouth borrows the sacred phrase in order to disarm the remaining conscience. One hears, underneath, the older warning that the greatest evils are those that arrive dressed as compassion and demand that resistance itself be named the sin.

The dung-skins come to change your nation. A ballot cast and it is all forfeit. They’ll rape your wives and kill your children. But just remember, Christ forgives. The image is deliberately ugly; the word is chosen to prevent aesthetic distance. The nation is not altered by argument but by replacement, and the replacement is presented as the moral test of those who would object. Lay down your weapons, it’s so progressive. Democratic, a mob to shiv. They’ll bleed you out and call it righteous. A sacrifice, such a life to live. The progressive is the one who progresses toward the knife and calls the bleeding justice. The philosophical tension is the ancient one between the many and the one, now staged as the many armed with the language of the one. Tocqueville’s soft despotism has acquired a harder edge: the administrative state no longer needs to convince when it can outvote, outnumber, and then forgive itself in advance.

Record it all and store the data. Let algorithms write the truth. The tech is money and money’s profit. A sea of censors hold no fools. Conspiracy are all the theorists. Just bow your heads and let prayer sooth. The AI god is without error. You’re out of credits, and that’s the proof. The final authority is no longer the priest or the politician but the system that scores and silences. Prayer is permitted only as the last private gesture before the credit runs out. The god does not err because error has been defined as dissent from its output. Here the poem touches the older fear of the idol that speaks and cannot be answered. The technological sublime is revealed as the technological final. One is invited to notice the precise moment one’s own thought begins to check itself against the anticipated score.

Fake "study groups" on WhatsApp are targeting people taking online AI courses. One currently uses my name and photo, plus IBM and Coursera logos, under the name "Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (AI). Study Group." A fake instructor promotes crypto trading "classes," members post screenshots of big gains, and people are asked to DM for "account setup."

Red flags:
• An AI course "instructor" adds you to a WhatsApp group or messages you directly.
• Any talk of crypto, trading profits, or "account setup."
• "Live classes" on meeting links outside the official course.

I never contact learners this way. Help with my tech courses happens in the official course discussion forums, and no legitimate instructor will ask you for money, wallet details, or personal information.

If you've been added to one of these groups, don't send anything, report the account in WhatsApp, and leave. If you've already shared something, contact your bank or exchange right away. Numbers used so far start with +44 but these can change.

With my courses past 1.1 million enrollments, I want every learner to see this. Please share it so it reaches others.
